Name: (AGD(AF)), FASL, and BCL2 combination
Developers: Zagazig University
Indication: Indicated for the diagnosis of Endometriosis.
Health care facility level: IVDs for Primary health care
Target: Anogenital distance from the upper verge of the anus to the posterior fourchette, FASL, and BCL2 combination.
Mechanism of action: Combines anogenital distance with apoptosis-related biomarkers (FASL, BCL2) to stratify likelihood of endometriosis.
Key features and challenges:
A 2024 study sought to investigate the anogenital distance from the upper verge of the anus to the posterior fourchette (AGDAF), FASL, and BCL2 combination as a reliable and non-invasive tool for the diagnosis of endometriosis.
The study included 100 women with endometriosis and 50 women without endometriosis as the control group. All cases underwent history taking, body mass index (BMI) measurement, AGD measurement, and FASL and BCL2 immunohistochemical staining of the eutopic endometrial tissue.
Endometriosis cases significantly had shorter AGDAF, 22.9 ± 2.6 mm, compared with the control group, 27.3 ± 3.5 mm (P < 0.001). Lower FASL and higher BCL2 expression were associated with endometriosis (P < 0.001). The combined measurement of AGDAF (cut-off point 24.55 mm) with FASL and BCL2 was associated with endometriosis (P < 0.001). The combined diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value of AGDAF, FASL, and BCL2 were 83%, 78%, 87.3%, and 69.6%, respectively. The area under the curve was greater for AGDAF, FASL, and BCL2 in combination than for individual measurements.
Combining short AGDAF with high BCL2 and low FASL is a highly sensitive, non-invasive diagnostic tool for endometriosis (https://obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ijgo.15412).

Name: 1,3-Dioxane-Linked novel bacterial topoisomerase inhibitors
Developers: The Ohio State University College of Medicine
Indication: Treatment of gonorrhoea
Mechanism of action: Inhibition of N. gonorrhoeae bacterial topoisomerase
Key features and challenges:
1,3-Dioxane-linked novel bacterial topoisomerase inhibitors (NBTIs) represent an investigational antibacterial class targeting bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. By stabilizing the enzyme–DNA cleavage complex, NBTIs disrupt DNA replication and transcription, leading to bacterial cell death. This mechanism is distinct from fluoroquinolones and is designed to overcome existing resistance pathways. Antimicrobial resistance in sexually transmitted infections, particularly Neisseria gonorrhoeae, has intensified the need for new therapeutic options.
In 2022, a study reported the synthesis and evaluation of two series of amine NBTIs bearing tricyclic DNA-binding moieties and amide NBTIs with bicyclic DNA-binding moieties (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9189870/). 
These compounds demonstrated potent in vitro activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Importantly, the dioxane-linked NBTIs and related bicyclic amine analogues also showed high antibacterial activity against both susceptible and drug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae, supporting expansion of this class into gonorrhea treatment research.
Key challenges include the preclinical stage of development, absence of human clinical trial data, and the need to demonstrate safety, pharmacokinetic suitability, and resistance durability in vivo. For gonorrhea specifically, optimal tissue penetration in urogenital and extragenital sites, as well as compatibility with combination therapy strategies, will be important considerations. Regulatory expectations for new antimicrobials in the context of resistance may also influence development pathways.
Overall, 1,3-dioxane-linked NBTIs represent a promising preclinical antibacterial class with demonstrated in vitro activity against drug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Advancement into clinical evaluation will be required to determine their potential role in addressing resistant gonorrhea.

Name: 1-D DUS
Developers: Maya Health Alliance Wuqu' Kawoq
Indication: Indicated for the detection of Preëclampsia
Health care facility level: IVDs for Primary health care
Mechanism of action: Ultrasound waves detect the motion and velocity of blood cells or cardiac structures along a single beam path
Key features and challenges:
One-dimensional Doppler ultrasound (1-D DUS) is a low-cost ultrasound technology designed to capture fetal heart tones and maternal–fetal hemodynamic signals using simplified hardware. It has been developed to expand access to prenatal screening in low-resource settings where conventional two-dimensional ultrasound is limited. Preliminary retrospective data suggest that 1-D DUS signals can be processed using artificial intelligence and deep-learning algorithms to estimate fetal gestational age, detect intrauterine growth restriction (FGR), and potentially predict maternal blood pressure–related disorders such as preeclampsia.
A 2024 prospective observational cohort study in rural Guatemala is evaluating the performance of 1-D DUS in predicting fetal growth restriction and preeclampsia (https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/14/9/e090503). The study plans to recruit 700 pregnant women before 18 6/7 weeks’ gestation and follow them through delivery and the early postpartum period. Trained nurses collect maternal weight, blood pressure, and 1-D DUS fetal heart recordings every four weeks. Participants also undergo three serial obstetric ultrasounds to assess fetal growth and a postpartum visit to document maternal and neonatal outcomes. The study will compare the predictive performance of deep-learning–derived 1-D DUS algorithms (using receiver operating characteristic curves) against standard two-dimensional ultrasound and established clinical risk prediction models for preeclampsia.
Key challenges include the need for external validation across diverse populations, robustness of artificial intelligence models in variable field conditions, and integration into referral pathways for timely management. While promising for low-resource environments, further evidence will be required to confirm accuracy, scalability, and cost-effectiveness relative to existing screening approaches.

Name: 1-methylpseudouridine–modified mRNA-LNP encoding MARV GP (Angola isolate)
Developers: University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston; University of Washington (including Harborview Medical Center)
Indication: Prevention of MVD (pre-exposure)
Mechanism of action: Intramuscular delivery of LNP-formulated mRNA leads to in vivo expression of MARV GP; induces neutralizing antibodies and Fc-mediated effector functions (ADCC, ADCP, ADNP) that block viral entry and eliminate infected cells.
Key features and challenges:
-Two-dose regimen in guinea pigs conferred 100% protection against lethal MARV challenge, with no viremia or disease signs.
-Also provided cross-protection against heterologous Ravn virus (RAVV) challenge.
-Differential antibody recognition: MARV vaccine induced strong glycan-cap–focused antibodies; RAVV vaccine induced stronger RBD/wing/GP2 recognition.
-Fc-effector functions (phagocytosis, NK activation) complement neutralization.
Recent updates:
-Builds on prior mRNA-LNP filovirus vaccine work: an EBOV GP mRNA-LNP showed full protection in guinea pigs.
-FDA-approved mRNA COVID-19 vaccines (e.g., Moderna, Pfizer/BioNTech) validate rapid pandemic deployment of this platform; MARV GP mRNA-LNP is positioned as a candidate for outbreak-driven clinical translation.
-Studies on lyophilized mRNA-LNP formulations for other pathogens show long-term thermostability at 4 °C, relevant for outbreak settings in Africa.
-RAVV cross-protection suggests potential for a bivalent Marburg/Ravn mRNA-LNP vaccine, currently under exploration by academic–industry consortia.

Name: 1-methylpseudouridine–modified mRNA-LNP encoding RAVV GP
Developers: University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston; University of Washington (including Harborview Medical Center)
Indication: Prevention of Ravn virus disease; cross-protection against Marburg virus
Mechanism of action: Intramuscular delivery of LNP-formulated mRNA induces GP expression, stimulating strong neutralizing antibodies and Fc-mediated effector functions (NK cytotoxicity, ADNP, ADCP), which block viral entry and clear infected cells.
Key features and challenges:
-Provided heterologous cross-protection against MARV challenge (complete survival, no viremia).
-Immune focus differs from MARV vaccine: RAVV mRNA-LNP induced more antibodies against RBD, wing, and GP2 regions of GP.
-Fc-effector responses (ADNK, ADCP, ADNP) enhanced after booster.
Recent updates:
-RAVV mRNA-LNP induced stronger autologous neutralization than MARV vaccine (higher homologous titers), though MARV vaccine gave stronger glycan-cap responses.
-Identified key linear epitopes in RBD and wing domains shared across MARV and RAVV, supporting bivalent or pan-marburgvirus vaccine design.
-Adds to the evidence that mRNA-LNP vaccines can generate sterilizing immunity against high-consequence filoviruses.
Provides a rationale for dual MARV + RAVV vaccine constructs, potentially advancing into NHP studies as the next translational step.

Name: 17-alpha-hydroxyprogesterone caproate  (oral) - PTL/PTB
Developers: Lipocine Inc.
Indication: Prevention of recurrent spontaneous preterm labour/birth
Mechanism of action: Reducing inflammation induced by placental ischemia
Key features and challenges:
Progesterone plays a central role in maintaining pregnancy. Although circulating progesterone levels remain elevated until term in humans, functional progesterone withdrawal occurs at labour onset due to alterations in progesterone receptor signaling. Injectable 17-alpha-hydroxyprogesterone caproate (17-OHPC) has been approved for prevention of recurrent spontaneous preterm birth in women with a prior singleton spontaneous PTB.
In 2015, the FDA granted Orphan Drug Designation to LPCN-1107 (developed by Lipocine), an oral formulation of 17-OHPC intended for prevention of PTL/PTB. The oral formulation was designed to address limitations associated with injectable and vaginal progesterone products, including invasiveness and adherence challenges, and aimed to become the first oral product for prevention of recurrent preterm birth.
A Phase I study conducted in healthy, non-pregnant female volunteers demonstrated significant oral absorption of LPCN-1107, with dose-proportional increases in maximum concentration and area under the curve. In January 2015, positive results were announced from a Phase Ib proof-of-concept study evaluating LPCN-1107 in pregnant women for prevention of preterm birth. In 2017, a pivotal Phase III study was announced in women with singleton pregnancies and a history of spontaneous PTL/PTB (https://adisinsight.springer.com/trials/700282603), although no subsequent public results have been reported.
A Phase II trial evaluating oral LPCN-1107 for prevention of preterm birth was underway in the USA as of April 2021, and Lipocine announced completion of Phase II in July 2021. However, detailed efficacy data have not been publicly released.
Key challenges include the broader regulatory controversy surrounding injectable 17-OHPC efficacy for recurrent PTB prevention, which may affect the development and approval pathway of oral formulations. While oral 17-OHPC offers potential advantages in administration and patient adherence, robust Phase III data demonstrating clear reduction in recurrent PTB and improvement in neonatal outcomes are required to establish clinical value.
Recent updates:
July 2021: Lipocine completes a Phase II trial in Preterm labour (Prevention) (Lipocine website, July 2021)

April 2021: Hydroxyprogesterone caproate oral is still in Phase II trials for preterm labour/birth prevention in USA (Lipocine pipeline).

2021: Evaluating Progestogens for Preventing Preterm birth International Collaborative (EPPPIC): meta-analysis of individual participant data from randomised controlled trials (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33773630/)

LPCN 1107 has been granted orphan drug designation by the FDA and has completed an end of Phase II meeting with the FDA in March, 2017.  Lipocine submitted a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) request with the US FDA in June 2017 for the design of the proposed Phase III trial for the prevention of recurrent preterm labour and the company received additional guidance from the US FDA regarding the design of a planned pivotal trial. This is confirmed from the official company (website https://www.lipocine.com/pipeline)

Name: 2-Methoxyestradiol
Developers: Johns Hopkins University (including the Bloomberg School of Public Health); The University of Texas Health Science Center
Indication: Uterine fibroid and lesion development
Mechanism of action: Anti-Angiogenic Activity: 2-ME inhibits the growth of new blood vessels (anti-angiogenic), which tumors need for oxygen and nutrient supply. This effect is particularly beneficial in restricting the growth of tumors, including fibroids.
Key features and challenges:
2-Methoxyestradiol (2-ME) is a natural metabolite of estradiol with anti-angiogenic, antiproliferative, and pro-apoptotic properties. Originally investigated as an anti-tumor agent, 2-ME inhibits microtubule function, disrupts cell cycle progression, suppresses angiogenesis, and promotes programmed cell death. These mechanisms are relevant to uterine fibroids (UF), which are characterized by excessive smooth muscle proliferation, extracellular matrix accumulation, and enhanced vascular support.
https://go.drugbank.com/drugs/DB02342

Despite its promising biological profile, clinical development of 2-ME has been limited by poor oral bioavailability, rapid metabolic degradation, and suboptimal pharmacokinetics. These limitations have prompted investigation of nanoparticle-based delivery systems to enhance stability, sustained release, and tumor targeting.
A 2023 study evaluated biodegradable PEG-PLGA nanoparticle formulations loaded with 2-ME in a patient-derived leiomyoma xenograft mouse model. The formulation achieved up to 99.1% encapsulation efficiency with minimal burst release. In vivo treatment resulted in a 51% reduction in tumor growth compared to controls, demonstrating significant antiproliferative activity in fibroid tissue.
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37482124/
In a related study, liposomal 2-ME nanoparticles administered via intraperitoneal injection in a leiomyoma mouse model produced significant tumor growth inhibition, with tumors 30.5% smaller than controls after two weeks of treatment (p = 0.025).
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43032-020-00248-w
While preclinical results support antifibroid activity, evidence remains limited to animal models. No human clinical trials have evaluated 2-ME formulations for uterine fibroids. Development challenges include optimization of delivery route, long-term safety, potential endocrine interactions given its estrogen-derived origin, and scalability of nanoparticle production.
2-Methoxyestradiol represents a mechanistically compelling antifibroid candidate targeting angiogenesis and cellular proliferation. However, its clinical utility in uterine fibroids remains investigational pending further pharmacokinetic optimization, toxicology studies, and human trials.
Recent updates: Sep 2023:  It was investigated in biodegradable and biocompatible 2-ME-loaded PEG-PLGA nanoparticles in a patient-derived leiomyoma xenograft mouse model. No other update since then

Name: 2-aminoethoxydiphenyl borate (2-APB)
Developers: University of Newcastle
Indication: for myometrial contraction blocking to prevent preterm birth
Mechanism of action: Ultrasound assessment of fetal cardiac structure and function to identify hemodynamic adaptations to growth restriction.
Key features and challenges:
2-aminoethoxydiphenyl borate (2-APB) is an organoboron compound that is diphenylborane in which the borane hydrogen is replaced by a 2-aminoethoxy group. It has a role as an IP3 receptor antagonist, a calcium channel blocker and a potassium channel opener. Since its introduction to Ca2+ signaling in 1997, 2-APB has been used in many studies to probe for the involvement of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors in the generation of Ca2+ signals. It is commonly used as a tool to modulate calcium signaling in physiological studies. While unspecific, 2-APB is one of the most-used agents to modulate store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) mediated by the STIM-gated Orai channels. Due to its boron core structure, 2-APB tends to readily hydrolyze in aqueous environment, a property that results in a complex physicochemical behavior. 

2-APB was originally introduced as an inhibitor of inositol trisphosphate (IP3) receptors (IP3R), which are a family of closely related Ca2+ channels embedded within the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR). However, subsequent studies in intact cells have revealed that 2-APB also inhibits Ca2+ entry via store-operated channels (SOC); an effect that is independent of IP3R inhibition. Thus, 2-APB has non-specific inhibitory effects on both IP3R and SOC, as well as on other Ca2+ transporters, e.g., sarcoplasmic Ca2+ ATPase (SRCA) pumps and transient receptor potential (TRP) channels of the TRPC family. 

Since its discovery, 2-APB has been tested on myometrial strips of rodents in several studies where it was found to inhibit both agonist-stimulated (OT, pennogenin tetraglycoside, Lannea acida plant extract, Ficus deltoidea plant extract) and spontaneous myometrial contractions. However, despite potently inhibiting pregnant rodent uterine contractility, the effects of 2-APB on spontaneous pregnant human myometrial contractions were yet to be examined.

In a 2022 study, myometrial strips obtained from term, not-in-labor women, and treated with cumulative concentrations of 2-APB in addition to other tocolytics. Comprehensive dose–response curves were then generated. A single treatment with each drug at the determined IC50 concentration was confirmed to reduce contraction performance (AUC) by approximately 50%. The overall order of contraction-blocking potency in decreasing order was nifedipine > rolipram > glycyl-H-1152 > HC-067047 > 2-APB > indomethacin > aminophylline.  This showed other tocolytics to have more potential than 2-APB. 
(https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43032-022-01000-2#author-information)

-Single-dose intraperitoneal administration protected against viremia, testicular atrophy, and epididymal damage in IFN-deficient (A6, AG6) mouse models.

Challenges:

Recent updates:
2025: 
-First demonstration that a single-dose 2B10 injection protected ZIKV-infected A6 and AG6 male mice from both reproductive tract damage and lethality.
-Showed restoration of testosterone and DHT levels to near-normal, preserving endocrine function in infected males.
-2B10 previously (2018) reported to protect against ZIKV-induced microcephaly in developing embryos, suggesting broad tissue-level protective capacity.

Key features and challenges: A scaffolded subunit immunogen (3AGJ) presenting the conserved membrane-proximal external region (MPER) of gp41 to elicit broadly-neutralising antibody responses. Given intramuscularly.
Recent updates: A 2026 study designed five killed whole-cell, genome-reduced bacterial vaccine constructs expressing versions of the scaffolded 3AGJ MPER antigen and confirmed their surface display using the broadly-neutralising antibody 2F5 (Viruses 2026, 18(2):209).

Name: 3D power doppler (3DPD) - PE
Developers: Universidad de La Laguna; Royal Victoria Hospital
Indication: Prediction of PE
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Target: Placental blood flow indices (Vascularization index, Flow Index, Vascularization Flow index, uterine artery pulsatility index)
Mechanism of action: Detects CD81 protein expression using optical biosensing to identify placental extracellular vesicle signatures associated with preeclampsia.
Key features and challenges:
Three-dimensional power Doppler is a 3D imaging technique which associates anatomical images (grayscale) with power Doppler signal. Power Doppler, compared to color Doppler, has the advantage of being based on the amplitude of the US signal and therefore of being little dependent on the insonation angle, less sensitive to the distraction or aliasing phenomena, and therefore more sensitive to detect very low velocity flows and smaller vessels. Combined with volume of interest (VOI) analysis, it should in theory be possible with the 3DPD technique to quantify the vascularisation directly within the utero-placental unit. 
 
Several studies have investigated the predictive power of 3D power Doppler for PE and found that in the first trimester, lower mean values of placental indices (vascularisation index, flow Index and vascularisation flow index) were significantly associated with subsequent development of PE (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0143400421006147). While there seems to be consistency in the direction of associations found in different studies, the sensitivity remains limited. One study for example found that the sensitivity of placental indices alone to predict early, late, and total PE was 23.1%, 18.3%, and 17.8% respectively. In association with all other variables (maternal characteristics, first trimester biomarkers, and uterine artery pulsatility index), the sensitivity increased to 84,6% for early preeclampsia, and 50 and 49.3% for late and total preeclampsia (https://karger.com/fdt/article-abstract/44/4/256/134712/Value-of-Placental-Volume-and-Vascular-Flow). 
 
It appears that 3D Power doppler can be an interesting tool to add to a multiparametric test for PE. The main limitation of 3DPD is its dependence to numerous technical or physiological parameters, influencing the calculated indices for the same observed blood flow. Some factors influencing the variability of these indices have been studied in vitro such as the flow intensity, the number of vessels and the haematocrit. The distance between the probe and the volume studied also has an impact, which implies that the body mass index, the position and the depth of the placenta can have an influence on the quantification of 3DPD indices.​

Name: 3D-printed condom intrauterine balloon tamponade
Developers: University of Warwick; University of Siena; Campus Biomedico of Rome
Indication: Indicated for the treatment of post-partum hemorrhage
Mechanism of action: Inflatable intrauterine balloon applies mechanical pressure to uterine walls to tamponade bleeding.
Key features and challenges: 2024 Study: results of a preclinical study aiming at informing the design, prototyping and validation of a 3D-printed intrauterine balloon tamponade concept, contributing towards the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goal 3: Good health and Well-being. Frugal engineering concepts and contextualised design techniques were applied throughout, to define the design requirements and specifications. The performance of the final prototype was validated against the requirements of the UK National Health System (NHS) technical guidelines and relevant literature, measuring the water leak and pressure drop over time, both open air and in a approximate uterus model. The resulting prototype is made up of six components, some of which are easy to retrieve, namely a water bottle, a silicone tube and an ordinary condom, while others can be manufactured locally using 3D printers, namely a modified bottle cap, a flow stopper and a valve for holding the condom in place. Validation testing bore promising results with no water or pressure leak open air, and minimal leaks in the approximate uterus model. This demonstrates that the 3D printed condom-based intrauterine balloon tamponade is performing well against the requirements and, when compared to the state of the art, it could be a more appropriate and more resilient solution to low-resource settings, as it bypasses the challenges in the supply of consumables and presents a greener option based on circular economy (https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0303844)

Name: 3STEP
Developers: Salus Discovery
Indication: Detection of gonorrhoea
Health care facility level: IVDs for Primary health care
Mechanism of action: Rapid point-of-care molecular assay detecting Neisseria gonorrhoeae nucleic acids to enable early identification of infection.
Key features and challenges:
Salus has invented 3STEP, a POC nucleic acid test (NAT) platform that enables laboratory performance at the point-of-care in a format that is as easy to perform as a rapid antigen test in <35 min using a single swab/sample. Laboratory performance in 3STEP is accomplished via exclusion-based sample preparation (ESP) for high-purity extraction/concentration. The single disposable device performs sample collection, nucleic acid extraction, and amplification/detection in spatially separated wells that enables rapid development of multiplexed test panels. The multiplexing capability of 3STEP allows for lab-quality POC single-visit testing and treatment for Chlamydia trachomatis (CT) and Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG). 
(https://reporter.nih.gov/search/kr8OWH9K5Umj1T1VEHoVjQ/project-details/10820325)

Name: 3xEIII
Developers: The Catholic University of Korea Seoul St. Mary's Hospital; GeneOne Life Science; Korea Institute of Science and Technology (KIST)
Indication: Prevention of ZIKV infection and congenital Zika syndrome.
Mechanism of action: Induces humoral and cellular immune responses by expressing three tandem repeats of E protein Domain III, generating neutralizing antibodies and memory T/B cells that block viral entry and replication.
Key features and challenges:

-Two intramuscular doses in mice elicited neutralizing antibodies (PRNT50 ~72.4 at 30 µg dose), robust memory B/T cell responses, and long-term protection up to 40 weeks.
-LNP-126 formulation improved safety and delivery (particle size ~102 nm, encapsulation efficiency ~83%).
-Antibody titers declined over time, but challenge at 40 weeks still showed reduced viral titers in organs.

Name: 4-aminoquinoline
Developers: University of Liverpool; Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine (LSTM)

Name: 4-hydroxy isoleucine
Developers: Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI)
Indication: Treatment of PCOS-related metabolic dysfunction
Mechanism of action: Glucose-Dependent Insulin Secretion stimulation; Activation of PI3 Kinase; Lipid lowering
Key features and challenges:
4-Hydroxyisoleucine (4-HIL) is a naturally occurring, non-proteinogenic amino acid derived from Trigonella foenum-graecum (fenugreek). The major stereoisomer (2S, 3R, 4S) exhibits insulinotropic and antidyslipidemic effects, enhancing glucose-dependent insulin secretion and reducing plasma triglycerides, cholesterol, and free fatty acids. These metabolic properties have generated interest in its potential application in obesity, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic syndrome—conditions closely linked to insulin resistance in PCOS.
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0223523417307341
Preclinical pharmacokinetic studies published in 2023 demonstrated that orally administered 4-HIL achieved approximately 56.8% absolute bioavailability in female Sprague–Dawley rats, with rapid systemic absorption and distribution to multiple tissues. The compound was detected in major organs and eliminated via urine and feces without evidence of acute toxicity in the tested model. These findings support its theoretical feasibility as an orally administered metabolic modulator and have prompted discussion of its potential relevance in PCOS, where insulin resistance and dyslipidemia are central features.
https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.4155/bio-2023-0074
Despite its promising metabolic profile, 4-hydroxyisoleucine remains an early-stage, preclinical candidate in the context of PCOS. No human clinical trials evaluating its effects on reproductive hormones, ovulatory function, androgen levels, or pregnancy outcomes in PCOS have been published to date. Mechanistic evidence linking 4-HIL directly to ovarian function or hyperandrogenism is limited, and optimal dosing, long-term safety, and formulation standardization have not been established. Additionally, as a bioactive compound derived from fenugreek, variability in extraction, purity, and stereoisomer composition may affect reproducibility and regulatory development pathways.

Name: 426c.Mod.Core-C4b + 3M-052-AF/Alum + HxB2.WT.Core-C4b + 3M-052-AF/Alum

Key features and challenges: A germline-targeting immunogen regimen of recombinant Env gp120-core constructs (426c and HxB2) with a 3M-052/alum adjuvant, designed to prime and guide maturation of broadly-neutralising antibody lineages against the gp120 core. Given intramuscularly.
Recent updates: A partially randomised, open-label Phase 1 trial (NCT06796686) began recruiting in 2025 to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of the prime-boost regimen.

Name: 426c.Mod.Core-C4b, 3M-052 AF + Alum
Developers: US National Institutes of Health (NIH); US National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Disease (NIAID); Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center (including the HIV Vaccine Trials Network (HVTN))

Name: 4CMenB
Developers: GSK; Norwegian Institute of Public Health (Folkehelseinstituttet); Novartis
Indication: protection against gonorrhoea
Mechanism of action: Immunostimulants - complement-mediated antibody-dependent killing of bacteria
Key features and challenges:
4CMenB (Bexsero®) is a broad-spectrum, recombinant protein vaccine licensed for protection against Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B disease. The vaccine contains outer membrane vesicles and recombinant antigens that share homology with Neisseria gonorrhoeae proteins, providing a biological rationale for potential cross-protection. Although there are currently no licensed vaccines specifically for gonorrhea, observational and laboratory-supported studies over the past decade have suggested that 4CMenB may confer partial protection, with estimates of 33–47% effectiveness against gonorrhea. Population-level data from mass vaccination campaigns in New Zealand and other countries using meningococcal B outer membrane vesicle vaccines have been associated with reduced reported rates of gonorrhea in vaccinated cohorts.
Modeling studies indicate that targeted 4CMenB vaccination strategies for populations at higher risk of gonorrhea could be both epidemiologically impactful and cost-saving. However, individuals infected with N. gonorrhoeae do not typically develop protective immunity against reinfection, and the correlates of immune protection remain incompletely understood. As such, prospective clinical evaluation is necessary to confirm protective efficacy.
Multiple clinical trials are currently investigating whether 4CMenB protects against acquisition of N. gonorrhoeae. These include:
NCT04094883 (started 2019) – https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04094883
NCT04297436 (started 2020) – https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04297436
NCT04350138 (started 2020) – https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04350138
NCT04415424 (started 2020) – https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04415424
NCT04722003 (started 2021) – https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04722003
NCT05294588 (started 2022) – https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05294588
NCT05766904 (started 2023) – https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05766904
NCT06446752 (started 2024) – https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06446752
In addition, NIH-supported research is evaluating immunologic and mechanistic aspects of meningococcal B vaccines in relation to gonorrhea prevention 
(Project ID 10832482; https://reporter.nih.gov/search/_HpqciuyRUep38K-3z0dfw/project-details/10832482).
Key challenges include the absence of definitive efficacy data from randomized controlled trials, uncertainty regarding duration and magnitude of protection, and variability in gonorrhea epidemiology across populations. Regulatory approval for a gonorrhea indication would require clear demonstration of protective efficacy, as current licensure is limited to meningococcal disease.
Overall, 4CMenB is a licensed meningococcal B vaccine with emerging observational and mechanistic evidence suggesting partial cross-protection against gonorrhea. Ongoing clinical trials will be critical in determining whether it can be formally positioned as a preventive strategy against N. gonorrhoeae.

Name: 4′-Fluorouridine (4′-FlU; EIDD-2749)
Developers: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); Utah State University; Emory Institute for Drug Development (EIDD)
Indication: Indicated for the treatment of LASV infection
Target: Viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (LASV L polymerase; arenavirus RdRp).
Mechanism of action: Incorporates into nascent viral RNA and causes transcriptional stalling/delayed chain termination by the viral polymerase, blocking RNA synthesis.
Key features and challenges:
-Broad-spectrum activity in vitro (incl. arenaviruses) and strong oral efficacy in vivo in lethal LASV and JUNV guinea-pig models.
-Therapeutic window includes late treatment starts (day 12 post-infection for LASV) with rapid clinical improvement; protection seen even at low dose (0.5 mg/kg).
-Class shows efficacy across RNA viruses (RSV, SARS-CoV-2, influenza, alphaviruses), supporting broad-spectrum positioning; watch for potential resistance pathways observed in influenza studies.
Recent updates:
2024-2025:
-CDC-led team and C&EN coverage summarizing LASV/JUNV findings.
-DHODH inhibitors reported to synergize with 4′-FlU in vitro.

Name: 5xM2e mRNA
Developers: Georgia State University (Including GSURF)
Indication: Indicated for active immunization against influenza A, caused by H1, H3, H5
Mechanism of action: Induces M2e-specific antibodies (driving Fc-mediated effector functions/ADCC) and T-cell responses; LNP also provides innate/adjuvant effects that enhance antibody magnitude and breadth; when co-administered, it boosts responses to inactivated split (HA) vaccine, improving homologous and heterologous protection.
Key features and challenges:
-Broad cross-subtype protection across H1/H3/H5 challenge models at low mRNA dose (≈1 µg) and robust GC/TFH responses.
-As a stand-alone M2e vaccine, efficacy is partial (weight-loss still occurs despite 100% survival); strongest performance seen when combined with inactivated split vaccine (sterilizing protection, sustained IgG & higher HAI).
Recent updates:
Sept 5, 2025:

Name: 6-methylmercaptopurine riboside (6MMpr)
Developers: University of Delhi (including ACBR, LHMC, Miranda House and UCMS)
Indication: Treatment of ZIKV infection

Key features and challenges:

-Good selectivity index (≈ 22.47).
-Minimal toxicity in acute/subacute oral dosing in mice (biochemical/histopathology shows negligible signs).

Small molecule hydroxyethylamine (HEA) analog (protease pharmacophore scaffold)

Name: 704/DNA vaccine
Developers: Institut Pasteur; Nantes Université
Indication: Prevention of ZIKV infection
Target: ZIKV non-structural proteins (NS1, NS3, NS4B, NS5, Capsid epitopes)
Mechanism of action: Induces CD8+ and CD4+ T-cell responses against ZIKV NS-derived epitopes; protection achieved in absence of neutralizing antibodies, thereby avoiding risk of antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE).
Key features and challenges:
-Promotes T-cell mediated immunity, overcoming ADE concerns associated with antibody-inducing vaccines.
-Demonstrated significant protection in HLA class I transgenic mice.
-No cross-protection against DENV2 despite some epitope sequence similarity.
-Limitation: efficacy data mainly in transgenic mice; lack of humoral immunity may restrict breadth of protection.
Recent updates:
Oct 2024 Publication: Study confirmed that ZIKV-NS poly-epitope DNA vaccine formulated with 704 induced strong T-cell responses and protection against ZIKV infection in HLA-A2402 and HLA-B0702 transgenic mice, without inducing neutralizing antibodies or ADE. 
-Protection was ZIKV-specific and not cross-protective against DENV2. Authors highlight the potential of multivalent DNA vaccines inducing T-cell immunity as an alternative to antibody-focused approaches.

Name: 8-bromobaicalein
Developers: University of Tsukuba; Chulalongkorn University (including the Asia Research Center, ARC)
Indication: Treatment of CHIKV infection and CHIKV-induced musculoskeletal inflammation
Target: CHIKV nsP1 methyltransferase (predicted primary target); possibly nsPs and E2 glycoprotein (secondary interactions)
Mechanism of action:
-In vitro: Inhibits CHIKV replication in Vero cells (EC₅₀ = 0.49 ± 0.11 µM).
-Molecular docking & FMO: Strong binding to GTP-binding pocket of nsP1; stabilizing interactions via bromine atom.
-In vivo: Oral administration (250 mg/kg, twice daily) alleviated CHIKV-induced musculoskeletal inflammation in mice, reduced viral RNA load, improved activity and swelling scores, and showed no hepatotoxicity or nephrotoxicity.
Key features and challenges:
-Features: Potent in vitro activity; in vivo efficacy in immunocompetent mouse model; favorable pharmacokinetic profile (oral Tmax ~1–2 h, t½ 4.6–6.4 h, plasma levels above EC₉₉.₉ maintained 12 h at 250 mg/kg).
-Safety: No hepatorenal toxicity observed at 250 mg/kg oral dosing; IV dosing caused mild ALT increase.
-Challenges: Limited to murine local infection model (not systemic); no NHP or human data yet; oral dosing requires high amounts; rapid metabolism with enterohepatic recirculation.
Recent updates:
June 2023:
-First CHIKV in vivo efficacy report for a flavone derivative 
-Cited in 2024–2025 reviews as a promising pan-arboviral lead. No clinical translation yet.

Name: A, C, Y, W135 meningococcal polysaccharide conjugate vaccine
Developers: Guangxi Autonomous Region Center for Disease Prevention and Control; China Air Force Medical University; Chinese National Institutes for Food and Drug Control; Sanjiang Center for Disease Control and Prevention; Simoon Record Pharma Information Consulting; Beijing Zhifei Lvzhu Biopharmaceutical
Indication: Indicated for active immunization against invasive meningococcal disease

Beijing Zhifei Lvzhu Biopharmaceutical, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Chongqing Zhifei Biological Products, is developing a polysaccharide conjugate vaccine againstmeningococcal groups A, C, Y and W-135 for which phase III clinical development has just began in China (NCT05252715).

The vaccine contains serogroup A, C, Y, and W135 polysaccharide antigens conjugated to Tetanus toxoids. Thevaccine provides protection only against meningococcalserogroups represented in the vaccine and will notprevent meningococcal infection caused by other serogroups (e.g., serogroup B) orby other pathogens.

In November 2019, Beijing Zhifei Lvzhu Biopharmaceutical completed a randomized, double-blind, parallel control, phase II study that evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of meningococcal ACYW-135 polysaccharide conjugate vaccine in healthy volunteers aged from 3 to 35 months (NCT05229536). Name: A16B1
Developers: National University of Rosario, Universidad Nacional de Rosario
Indication: Indicated for the treatment of Salmonella infections
Mechanism of action: Inhibits the Salmonella PhoP/PhoQ system.
Key features and challenges:
The upsurge of antimicrobial resistance demands innovative strategies to fight bacterial infections. With traditional antibiotics becoming less effective, anti-virulence agents or pathoblockers, arise as an alternative approach that seeks to disarm pathogens without affecting their viability, thereby reducing selective pressure for the emergence of resistance mechanisms.

Objectives
To elucidate the mechanism of action of compound N′-(thiophen-2-ylmethylene)benzohydrazide (A16B1), a potent synthetic hydrazone inhibitor against the Salmonella PhoP/PhoQ system, essential for virulence.

Materials and methods
The measurement of the activity of PhoP/PhoQ-dependent and -independent reporter genes was used to evaluate the specificity of A16B1 to the PhoP regulon. Autokinase activity assays with either the native or truncated versions of PhoQ were used to dissect the A16B1 mechanism of action. The effect of A16B1 on Salmonella intramacrophage replication was assessed using the gentamicin protection assay. The checkerboard assay approach was used to analyse potentiation effects of colistin with the hydrazone. The Galleria mellonella infection model was chosen to evaluate A16B1 as an in vivo therapy against Salmonella.

Results
A16B1 repressed the Salmonella PhoP/PhoQ system activity, specifically targeting PhoQ within the second transmembrane region. A16B1 demonstrates synergy with the antimicrobial peptide colistin, reduces the intramacrophage proliferation of Salmonella without being cytotoxic and enhances the survival of G. mellonella larvae systemically infected with Salmonella.

Conclusions
A16B1 selectively inhibits the activity of the Salmonella PhoP/PhoQ system through a novel inhibitory mechanism, representing a promising synthetic hydrazone compound with the potential to function as a Salmonella pathoblocker. This offers innovative prospects for combating Salmonella infections while mitigating the risk of antimicrobial resistance emergence

(https://academic.oup.com/jac/article-abstract/79/8/1820/7690286?redirectedFrom=fulltext).

The purpose of this randomized, double-blind clinical trial is to optimize ALFQ dosing.

Name: A27L, VACV A33R, L1R, and B5R Subunit / Recombinant Vaccines
Developers: Bridging Health Foundation
Indication: Prophylactic Prevention of Mpox infection
Target: A27L (IMV fusion protein), A33R (EEV membrane protein), L1R (IMV membrane protein), B5R (EEV glycoprotein)
Mechanism of action: Induces neutralizing antibodies and T-cell responses against both IMV and EEV forms of orthopoxviruses, blocking viral entry and spread.
Key features and challenges:
-Each antigen contributes differently: L1R and B5R confer strong protection, A33R enhances EEV immunity, A27L supports IMV neutralization.
-Combinations (e.g., L1R + A33R + B5R) provide more robust immunity than single antigens.
-Protection shown in animal models (mice, primates) against vaccinia/mpox challenge.
-Need for optimized adjuvants and clinical development.
Recent updates: These four proteins remain the “core antigen set” for next-gen mpox vaccines, forming the basis of multivalent mRNA, DNA, and nanoparticle vaccines (e.g., MPXVac-097, Lmix6).

Name: A29/B6/M1
Developers: China CDC
Indication: Prevention of mpox disease in at-risk populations
Target: MPXV antigens A29L (IMV; A27 homolog), B6R (EEV; A33 homolog), M1R (IMV; L1 homolog)
Mechanism of action: Induces antigen-specific humoral and cellular immunity; M1 drives neutralizing antibodies to block IMV entry, while A29/B6 elicit strong T-cell responses and EEV/IMV coverage, together reducing viral replication and pathology; confers cross-protection vs orthopoxviruses in mice.
Key features and challenges:
-Complete protection in mice against high-dose VACV-WR and ECTV when given as A29/B6/M1 (Alum+CpG), with reduced lung viral load and milder pathology; A29/B6 alone only partially protective, and adding A35 did not improve outcomes in this model.
-Suggests complementary roles of neutralizing antibodies (M1-dependent) and A29/B6-specific cellular immunity; correlates of protection identified.
Challenges: Potential antigen-competition effects and A35 conformational issues noted in the preclinical study.
Recent updates:
-Antigen conservation & rationale: Independent analyses show very high homology across clades, including 100% identity for B6R and M1R between clade IIb and clade I sequences—supporting cross-clade utility of the A29/B6/M1 antigen set. 
-Platform corroboration: Multiple platforms (mRNA, nanoparticles, DNA) using the same four canonical antigens (A29, B6, M1, A35) report strongest protection when M1 is included and when IMV+EEV antigens are combined—consistent with the A29/B6/M1 design emphasis on M1 for neutralization plus EEV/IMV breadth. 
-Microneedle DNA subunits: 2025 data show multicomponent MPXV DNA vaccines encoding A29L, B6R, M1R, A35R delivered by microneedles elicited robust responses—supporting the same antigen constellation’s translatability across platforms/delivery tech. 
-Antibody science: 2025 studies isolated/characterized human or murine antibodies to M1R and B6R, underscoring these as key neutralizing targets relevant to this trivalent’s MoA and potential for serological correlates/biomarkers

Name: A29L mRNA-LNP vaccine
Developers: Tecnologico de Monterrey, Campus Querétaro; University of Oslo
Indication: Prophylactic
Mechanism of action: Induces A29L-specific humoral and cellular responses to block virion entry
Key features and challenges: Strong immunogenicity in mice; protection assessed with VACV challenge; need MPXV challenge/NHP data

Name: A35R-M1R-B6R Trivalent mRNA Vaccine (AMAB/AMB variants)
Developers: Tsinghua University
Indication: Prevention of mpox infection
Target: MPXV A35R (EEV glycoprotein), M1R (IMV membrane protein), B6R (EEV glycoprotein).
Mechanism of action: Encodes a single-chain chimeric immunogen combining soluble domains of A35R, M1R, and B6R; induces neutralizing antibodies and T-cell responses against both intracellular mature virus (IMV) and extracellular enveloped virus (EEV), blocking viral entry, spread, and replication.
Key features and challenges:
-Novel single-chain design simplifies vaccine manufacturing compared to multi-mRNA cocktails.
-Elicited potent humoral and cellular immunity in mice with high neutralizing antibody titers against both VACV and MPXV.
-Complete protection (100%) against lethal doses of VACV in mice; significantly reduced viral loads in lungs, ovaries, and spleen after MPXV challenge.
-Outperformed both live-attenuated VACV Tian Tan (VACV-VTT) and A35R+M1R+B6R cocktail vaccines.
-Long-term antibody persistence observed up to day 166 post-vaccination.
Recent updates:
-This vaccine candidate represents one of the first successful single-chain mRNA mpox vaccines with evidence of both robust neutralization and complete protection in mice.
-Compared to multi-antigen cocktails, it reduces complexity, improves quality control, and lowers production costs.
-Developers have filed patent applications for AMAB-wt, AMAB-C140S, and AMB-C140S variants.

Name: A38-mRNA-LNP
Developers: ZJU-Hangzhou Global Scientific and Technological Innovation Center; Zhejiang University
Indication: Treatment or prevention of RVFV infection in humans/animals
Mechanism of action: In vivo–expressed A38 IgG binds Gn and blocks membrane fusion/entry, neutralizing virus.
Key features and challenges:
-Rapid in vivo expression and prolonged serum exposure vs protein dosing; t½ ~3–18 days in mice, Tmax ~3 days (dose-dependent).
-PK demonstrated; pharmacodynamics/efficacy for the mRNA product not yet shown (A38 protein itself previously protective in mice).
-Needs immunogenicity/toxicology, dose optimization (high dose shortened duration), and route/formulation studies.
Recent updates:
-Literature indexing confirms the PK paper (Jan 2024) with no subsequent peer-reviewed in vivo efficacy publications for A38-mRNA-LNP specifically as of Sept 16, 2025.
-Related field signals (not the same product): continued progress on RVFV mRNA vaccines (e.g., LNP-saRNA Gn/Gc in mice, 2024) and CEPI-funded Afrigen human mRNA RVFV vaccine program (2025). These indicate ecosystem momentum but are distinct from A38-mRNA-LNP.

Name: AAV6.2FF-FVM04-MR191

Name: ABt140
Developers: Abalone Bio
Indication: Treatment of endometriosis associated pain, inflammation and fibrosis
Mechanism of action: Cannabinoid 2 receptor agonist
Key features and challenges:
Cannabinoid 2 receptors (CB2) are emerging as a promising target for the treatment of endometriosis. CB2 is predominantly expressed in immune cells, nociceptive neurons, and peripheral structural cells, such as epithelial cells and myofibroblasts, including those in uterine tissue. Activation of CB2 receptors reduces excessive inflammation and fibrosis without hindering beneficial inflammatory responses, such as those against pathogens or adaptive humoral B-cell responses. While several companies have developed small molecule CB2 agonists, these compounds are often rapidly cleared, can penetrate the blood-brain barrier, and may have off-target effects mediated by CB1 receptors, including cognitive side effects. Abalone Bio has utilized its proprietary Functional Antibody Selection Technology (FAST) to isolate a selective CB2-activating nanobody (VHH), which has been developed into a VHH-Fc fusion lead antibody, ABt140. ABt140 is anticipated to be a highly specific, long-lasting, peripherally restricted CB2 receptor agonist antibody therapy for endometriosis, aimed at reversing or mitigating peritoneal inflammation and fibrosis, and alleviating abdominal pain. Initial proof of concept has been demonstrated in mouse models of pain, inflammation, and fibrosis.

Abalone Bio received NIH funding in 2022 to conduct a Phase 1 study to validate the CB2 antibody agonist concept as an effective strategy for painful endometriosis through three complementary and non-overlapping objectives; confirm in vitro that the CB2 antibody agonist is efficacious for endometriosis; demonstrate that the drug’s efficacy in mouse models is due to mechanisms relevant to human endometriosis;  improve the stability of the lead antibody to create a commercially and clinically viable candidate. If these aims are successful, the next steps will include implementing additional animal models in larger animals, further advancing the antibody drug toward investigational new drug (IND)-enabling studies and initial human trials. (https://legacy.www.sbir.gov/sbirsearch/detail/2338665)

Name: AD-01
Developers: University of Technology Sydney
Indication: Indicated for the treatment of Preeclampsia
Mechanism of action: Inhibits NF-κB signaling, reducing production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (such as IL-6 and TNF-α) that contribute to vascular damage.
Key features and challenges:
AD-01 is an investigational therapeutic candidate evaluated for its potential to mitigate placental oxidative stress and inflammation in preeclampsia (PE). Preeclampsia is characterized by endothelial dysfunction, angiogenic imbalance, and placental oxidative injury. Elevated circulating uric acid (UA) and malondialdehyde (MDA), a marker of lipid peroxidation, are frequently observed in women with PE and reflect systemic and placental oxidative stress.
A 2025 study assessed UA and MDA concentrations in plasma samples from women with preeclampsia (n = 24) compared with normotensive controls (n = 14) using colorimetric assays (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cell-and-developmental-biology/articles/10.3389/fcell.2025.1539496/full). 
MDA levels were significantly increased in the PE group (p < 0.001), and UA showed a significant association with PE after adjustment for gestational age (p = 0.03). The study further employed a two-dimensional in vitro first-trimester trophoblast model (ACH-3P cell line) exposed to PE-like stressors including hypoxia mimic (DMOG), inflammatory stimulus (TNF-α), and mitochondrial dysfunction agent (Rhodamine-6G). These stimuli induced increases in UA and/or MDA concentrations and impaired trophoblast proliferation and migration, modeling features of abnormal placentation.
Treatment with AD-01 (100 nM) abrogated TNF-α–induced increases in UA and Rho-6G/DMOG-induced increases in MDA (p < 0.001–0.0001). In addition, AD-01 restored trophoblast proliferation, migration, and reduced inflammatory signaling under PE-like conditions, with effects comparable to aspirin, metformin, and resveratrol (p < 0.05). These findings suggest that AD-01 may exert protective effects by attenuating oxidative and inflammatory pathways implicated in PE pathophysiology.
Key challenges include the exclusively in vitro nature of the evidence, limiting conclusions regarding in vivo efficacy and safety in pregnancy. Dose optimization, pharmacokinetics, placental transfer characteristics, and maternal–fetal safety profiles remain undefined. Additionally, the complexity of PE pathogenesis—encompassing immunologic, vascular, and angiogenic components—requires validation of therapeutic benefit in animal models and ultimately in controlled clinical trials. While AD-01 demonstrates promising antioxidant and cytoprotective effects in trophoblast models, translational research is necessary to establish its clinical relevance in preeclampsia management.

Name: AFP/PAPP-A ratio - PE
Developers: University of Cambridge; Kyung Hee University
Indication: Prediction of PE
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Target: Ratio of levels of Pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A) and Alpha fetoprotein (AFP) in serum to predict PE
Mechanism of action: Immunoassays identify and quantify the AFP/PAPP-A ratio in maternal serum
Key features and challenges:
Pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A) and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) are established maternal serum biomarkers routinely measured during prenatal screening. Low first-trimester PAPP-A levels have been associated with placental dysfunction and adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preeclampsia (PE). In a 2020 study, elevated second-trimester AFP, primarily produced by the fetal liver, has also been linked to placental disorders; however, predictive performance for PE when used alone has generally been limited (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32050927/).
The Pregnancy Outcome Prediction study evaluated the combined AFP/PAPP-A ratio in a large prospective cohort of 4,057 nulliparous women (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31138428/). An AFP/PAPP-A ratio greater than 10 was associated with increased risk of placentally related adverse outcomes, including fetal growth restriction (RR 3.74, 95% CI 2.30–6.09), severe preeclampsia (RR 2.12, 95% CI 1.39–3.25), and stillbirth (RR 5.05, 95% CI 1.48–17.18). The combined ratio demonstrated improved predictive performance compared with either biomarker alone and performed equivalently to multivariable models combining both markers. Predictive accuracy was not materially influenced by correction for maternal weight or gestational age at sampling.
A subsequent 2022 study further supported the enhanced predictive value of the AFP/PAPP-A ratio for PE, reporting an optimal cut-off of >6.89 with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.783, outperforming individual biomarkers (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9771328/).
Key challenges include variability in optimal ratio cut-offs across studies, moderate overall predictive performance, and the need for validation in diverse populations. While the AFP/PAPP-A ratio may enhance early risk stratification for placental dysfunction and preeclampsia, integration into screening algorithms would require prospective validation and assessment of incremental value over established multimarker models.

Mechanism of action: Applies machine learning to ultrasound-derived cervical and uterine features to generate risk predictions for impending preterm labour.
Key features and challenges: A proprietary AI software was written and trained on a set of de-identified ultrasound images from a retrospective cohort of women who delivered at the University of Kentucky from 2017 to 2021. Data from 4,505 patients (79% of this cohort) was used to train the AI to optimise prediction for preterm birth < 37 weeks (15,634 unique ultrasound studies and 757,050 total images). Specific anatomic locations (“hot spots”) were identified which provided discrimination for prediction. Hot spots included the cervix, lower uterine segment, amniotic fluid, decidual thickness and vascularisation, placental location, and select fetal anatomy. The date of the exam and ultrasound imaging alone were utilised to suggest whether that specific patient would be expected to deliver preterm (< 37 weeks GA) or < 30 days from the examination. Preterm birth rates in the training set (18.4%) and validation set (18.6%) were similar. Results conclude that AI can predict preterm delivery via ultrasound, and AI can simultaneously combine multiple sources of information into one prediction (https://www.ajog.org/article/S0002-9378(22)01823-3/fulltext).

Name: AI-PREMie

Target: Three patent-pending biomarkers of PE in plasma analyzed by AI for determination of risk
Mechanism of action: Machine learning is used to identify "molecular signatures" by integrating clinical data with a novel platelet-based biomarker platform
Key features and challenges:
AI-PREMie is an artificial intelligence–powered risk stratification tool designed to support diagnosis and severity prediction of preeclampsia (PE). The platform is based on biomarker discovery research using the PALADIN platelet-based technology platform, which identified a combination of patent-pending biomarkers associated with PE and provisional disease severity. The proposed diagnostic approach involves measurement of three novel plasma biomarkers, integrated into an AI-driven predictive algorithm (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/prca.201800162).
AI-PREMie aims to provide earlier and more precise identification of women at risk of developing PE and to stratify patients according to severity, potentially supporting triage, monitoring, and management decisions. The platform leverages computational analysis of biomarker patterns rather than reliance on single-marker thresholds. Additional information on development and positioning is available via the developer’s website (https://aipremie.com/).
Key challenges include limited publicly available peer-reviewed clinical validation data, unclear regulatory status, and the need for external validation in diverse populations. Demonstration of diagnostic accuracy, comparative performance versus established biomarkers (e.g., sFlt-1/PlGF ratio), and integration into clinical workflows will be critical to establish clinical utility and adoption.

Name: AI-supported ultrasound diagnostic

Key features and challenges: Researchers at Huazhong University of Science and Technology are working on a new AI-assisted method to help junior ultrasonographers improve their ability to diagnose uterine fibroids. In a 2023 retrospective study, they analyzed 3,870 ultrasound images from 667 patients with a confirmed diagnosis of uterine fibroids (average age 42.45 ± 6.23 years) and 570 women without uterine lesions (average age 39.24 ± 5.32 years), collected at Shunde Hospital of Southern Medical University between 2015 and 2020. Its performance was then tested on an external set of 488 images, comparing results with ultrasonographers of varying experience levels. With AI support, junior ultrasonographers achieved significantly higher accuracy (94.72% vs. 86.63%), sensitivity (92.82% vs. 83.21%), specificity (97.05% vs. 90.80%), positive predictive value (97.45% vs. 91.68%), and negative predictive value (91.73% vs. 81.61%) than they did alone. Their performance was on par with that of senior ultrasonographers across all metrics (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-26771-1)

Name: ARV-110
Developers: Arvinas
Indication: Treatment of PCOS
Mechanism of action: Androgen receptor degradation enhancers
Key features and challenges:
ARV-110 is a novel Proteolysis Targeting Chimera (PROTAC) androgen receptor (AR) degrader originally developed for prostate cancer. Unlike traditional androgen receptor antagonists that block receptor activity, ARV-110 promotes proteasomal degradation of AR protein, thereby suppressing AR-mediated transcriptional signaling. This targeted protein degradation approach offers a mechanistically distinct strategy that may reduce persistent androgen signaling more effectively than conventional AR blockade.
Given the central role of hyperandrogenism in the pathophysiology of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), ARV-110 has emerged as a potential therapeutic candidate for androgen-mediated complications in this condition. Traditional AR blockers in women are limited by safety concerns and tolerability issues, including hepatotoxicity and teratogenicity. ARV-110’s selective degradation mechanism may provide a safer alternative, although this remains to be clinically validated.
A 2023 published preclinical study evaluated ARV-110 in a dihydrotestosterone (DHT)-induced hyperandrogenemic mouse model of PCOS. DHT-treated mice developed increased body weight, adiposity, renal enlargement, impaired glucose tolerance, and elevated markers of renal injury and extracellular matrix remodeling. ARV-110 treatment reduced renal AR protein levels by approximately 70% and reversed DHT-induced metabolic and renal abnormalities, including improvements in body composition, glucose regulation, and kidney injury markers. These findings suggest potential utility in mitigating androgen-driven metabolic and organ dysfunction in PCOS.
However, evidence remains limited to preclinical models, and no clinical trials in women with PCOS have been reported to date. Further translational and clinical studies are required to establish safety, reproductive effects, and long-term metabolic outcomes before therapeutic positioning in PCOS can be defined.

Name: ATSB®
Developers: Innovative Vector Control Consortium (IVCC); University of Bamako (including University of Science, Techniques and Technology Bamako (USTTB) and WANECAM); Westham Co.
Indication: Prevention and control of malaria in children and adults living in areas with ongoing malaria transmission.
Mechanism of action: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) competitive modulator
Key features and challenges:
Currently under Vector Control Advisory Group (VCAG) review for assessment of public health value as of March 2020.Three IVCC-sponsored RCT protocols reviewed by VCAG in May 2019. Trials are expected to take place in Mali, Zambia and Kenya between 2021 and 2024.

ATSB (Attractive Toxic Sugar Baits) is an innovative vector control method designed to target malaria-transmitting mosquitoes by leveraging their natural sugar-feeding behavior. Both male and female mosquitoes feed on sugar for energy, and ATSBs combine sugar baits with a lethal toxin to attract and kill them. By targeting mosquitoes before they can transmit diseases, ATSBs help reduce vector populations and lower the risk of malaria transmission.  

Environmentally friendly and selective, ATSBs are designed to minimize harm to non-target species, such as pollinators, while effectively controlling mosquito populations. They are typically deployed outdoors in strategic locations where mosquitoes are likely to feed on sugar sources, making them a complementary tool to traditional methods like insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) and indoor residual spraying (IRS).  

However, challenges remain, including ensuring the safety of non-target species, demonstrating consistent field effectiveness in diverse environmental conditions, and gaining community acceptance of this novel approach. Additionally, sustained monitoring will be required to prevent resistance to the toxins used in ATSBs.  

Despite these challenges, ATSBs represent a promising tool in the fight against malaria, particularly in outdoor transmission settings where existing control methods are less effective. By integrating ATSBs into broader vector control programs, they could play a significant role in reducing the global burden of mosquito-borne diseases.
Recent updates:
Discussed at the eighteenth meeting of the WHO Vector Control Advisory Group (April 2023).
Phase III efficacy trial study results published in 2024 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39548456/).
Community acceptance trial in Zambia results published in 2024 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39129018/).

Name: AVACC-11
Developers: Therapyx; Intravacc
Indication: Prevention of gonorrhoea
Target: Outer Membrane Vesicles (OMV) from N. gonorrhoeae
Mechanism of action: It incorporates Outer Membrane Vesicles (OMV) from N. gonorrhoeae to stimulate the production of immunoglobulins A and G (IgA, IgG) from airway mucosal cells. Co-administered sustained-release microspheres containing human interleukin-12 (IL-12) counteract immune suppression typically seen in N. gonorrhoeae infection
Key features and challenges:
AVACC-11 is an investigational intranasal vaccine candidate developed by Intravacc for the prevention of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection. The vaccine is based on an outer membrane vesicle (OMV) platform designed to induce robust mucosal and systemic immune responses, including immunoglobulin A (IgA) and immunoglobulin G (IgG) production. AVACC-11 incorporates sustained-release microspheres containing human interleukin-12 (IL-12) to enhance Th1-driven immune responses and counteract the immune evasion mechanisms associated with gonococcal infection. The OMV-Vacc platform has previously been applied to other prophylactic vaccine candidates (https://www.intravacc.nl/services/pipeline/avacc-vaccine-candidates).
Earlier preclinical work demonstrated that an OMV-based gonococcal vaccine combined with microsphere-encapsulated IL-12, administered intravaginally, elicited systemic, mucosal, and T-cell (Th1) immune responses. Following vaginal challenge with N. gonorrhoeae, vaccinated animals exhibited resistance to infection. However, the intravaginal route was considered impractical for broad human application, prompting development of an intranasal formulation to enhance acceptability and applicability across sexes (https://journals.asm.org/doi/epub/10.1128/msphere.00388-22
; https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/intravacc-announces-favorable-preclinical-data-for-its-candidate-intranasal-gonorrhea-vaccine-avacc-11-301722085.html).
Preclinical studies in murine and non-human primate models have supported further advancement of the intranasal candidate. The U.S. NIH/NIAID has awarded Intravacc a contract to develop AVACC-11 through Phase I clinical evaluation. As of March–April 2024, the candidate remains in preclinical development, with plans to initiate a Phase I trial in gonorrhea prevention in 2025 (https://adisinsight.springer.com/drugs/800046754; https://www.intravacc.nl/fileadmin/01Website/Downloads/Vaccsheet/Avacc11_Gonorrhea_0923_LR.pd).
Key challenges include translation of preclinical immunogenicity and protection data into durable human efficacy, identification of immune correlates of protection against gonorrhea, and navigation of regulatory pathways for a first-in-class gonococcal vaccine. Demonstration of safety and mucosal immune durability in early-phase trials will be critical.
Overall, AVACC-11 represents a novel OMV-based intranasal vaccine strategy targeting gonorrhea prevention with encouraging preclinical results. Progression to Phase I clinical testing will determine its feasibility and immunogenicity in humans.

Name: Acarbose
Developers: Université de Sherbrooke; RenJi Hospital; Bayer Healthcare
Indication: Treatment of PCOS-related metabolic dysfunction and hyperandrogenism
Mechanism of action: Competitively and reversibly inhibits both pancreatic alpha-amylase and membrane-bound alpha-glucosidases
Key features and challenges:
Acarbose is an oral alpha-glucosidase inhibitor that delays the intestinal absorption of complex carbohydrates, thereby suppressing postprandial glucose and insulin excursions. By reducing post-meal hyperinsulinemia, acarbose may indirectly attenuate insulin-driven ovarian androgen production, a central feature of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/03007995.2024.2358237
Several meta-analyses have evaluated acarbose in women with PCOS. A 2021 systematic review reported improvements in metabolic and endocrine parameters, including reductions in testosterone, triglycerides, and very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL), along with increases in high-density lipoprotein (HDL).
https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/ijamh-2021-0073/html
A 2022 meta-analysis further confirmed reductions in androgen levels and improvements in lipid profiles with acarbose treatment in PCOS populations.
https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/24/8/7454
Additional evidence demonstrated that acarbose significantly reduced mean body weight, body mass index (BMI), and waist circumference compared with placebo, supporting its potential benefit in overweight and insulin-resistant PCOS phenotypes.
https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/cen.14663
An ongoing randomized clinical trial (NCT01019356) is comparing 8 weeks of rosiglitazone versus acarbose in lean and obese women with PCOS to assess reversal of insulin-related hyperandrogenism. The study is based on the hypothesis that free fatty acid accumulation contributes to insulin resistance and androgen excess in PCOS.
https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01019356
Another non-randomized clinical study (NCT02446834) is evaluating intensive lifestyle intervention combined with pharmacologic agents—including GLP-1 receptor agonists, metformin, and acarbose—in overweight and obese women with PCOS and early-onset diabetes.
https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02446834
Although acarbose demonstrates metabolic and androgen-lowering effects, it is not universally guideline-endorsed as a first-line therapy for PCOS. Gastrointestinal side effects, including flatulence and abdominal discomfort, may limit tolerability. Its primary benefit appears confined to metabolic and insulin-related aspects of PCOS rather than direct ovulation induction. Additionally, comparative effectiveness relative to metformin or GLP-1 receptor agonists remains incompletely defined in contemporary treatment algorithms.
Overall, acarbose represents a metabolically targeted adjunct therapy for PCOS, with evidence supporting improvements in insulin resistance, lipid profile, androgen levels, and anthropometric measures. However, its role in routine PCOS management remains secondary to more widely adopted insulin-sensitizing or weight-reduction agents pending further high-quality comparative trials.

Name: Acetate - PCOS
Developers: Afe Babalola University
Indication: PCOS inflammation, oxidative stress, lipid/glucose homeostasis, and fertility
Target: Histones; Metabolism; Inflammation; Neurons; Hormones; Lipids
Mechanism of action: Histone Acetylation; Energy Metabolism; Regulation of Inflammation; Neuroprotection; Metabolic Regulation; Hormonal and Lipid Profile Regulation
Key features and challenges:
Acetate is the conjugate base of acetic acid and a naturally occurring short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) metabolite produced endogenously and by intestinal microbiota fermentation. It functions as a systemic metabolic substrate and signaling molecule and has been implicated in modulation of inflammation, epigenetic regulation, and energy homeostasis.
https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Acetate#section=2D-Structure
Preclinical studies in rodent models of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) have explored acetate as a metabolic and anti-inflammatory modulator. A 2022 study demonstrated that acetate mitigated depressive-like behavior and neuroinflammation in PCOS rats by suppressing DNA methylation and histone deacetylase 2 (HDAC2) expression in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus.
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12035-022-03074-0
Subsequent research showed that acetate alleviated adipose–hepatic metabolic dysregulation by reducing androgen excess and suppressing NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome activation. These effects were associated with improvements in lipid profiles, glycogen synthesis, and antioxidant defenses in hepatic and adipose tissues.
https://cdnsciencepub.com/doi/10.1139/cjpp-2023-0169
Additional 2022 findings reported that acetate mitigated renal dysfunction in PCOS models by reducing oxidative stress, apoptosis, androgen excess, and inflammatory signaling via NF-κB/NLRP3 pathways. Restoration of hypothalamic–adipose kisspeptin signaling was also observed, suggesting effects on reproductive-endocrine regulation.
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12020-022-03191-9
Further mechanistic work demonstrated that acetate alleviated cardiac mitochondrial dysfunction by modulating GPCR41/43 signaling, increasing PROKR1 expression, and improving mitochondrial performance. In skeletal muscle, acetate enhanced metabolic flexibility by reducing oxidative stress and histone deacetylase activity and suppressing PDK4 and NLRP3 inflammasome pathways.
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0899900722003264?via%3Dihub
Most recently, a 2024 study reported that acetate improved ovarian mitochondrial dysfunction and normalized reproductive endocrine profiles in PCOS rats, potentially via modulation of mitofusin-2 (MFn2), suggesting direct ovarian cellular benefits.
https://jps.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12576-024-00908-5
Collectively, these findings indicate that acetate may exert multi-system effects in PCOS models, including modulation of inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, androgen excess, and neuroendocrine signaling.
However, all current evidence is preclinical and derived from animal models. No human clinical trials evaluating acetate supplementation for PCOS have been reported. The translational relevance of dosing, route of administration, and systemic acetate levels in humans remains uncertain. Additionally, acetate is a broadly acting metabolite rather than a targeted pharmacologic agent, which may complicate regulatory classification and therapeutic standardization.

Mechanism of action: Unknown
Key features and challenges:
Acetazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor traditionally used in the management of conditions such as glaucoma, epilepsy, and altitude sickness. Recent research has explored its potential repositioning as an antibacterial agent against Neisseria gonorrhoeae, the causative pathogen of gonorrhea. Carbonic anhydrases are essential for bacterial physiology, and inhibition of these enzymes represents a non-traditional antimicrobial strategy distinct from current first-line gonococcal therapies.
In 2022, a preclinical study evaluated acetazolamide for anti-gonococcal activity (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0882401022000675). 
The compound demonstrated potent in vitro activity and significantly reduced vaginal gonococcal burden by approximately 90% within three days in an infected murine model. These findings suggest that targeting bacterial carbonic anhydrases may represent a viable adjunctive or alternative therapeutic pathway, particularly in the context of increasing antimicrobial resistance.
Key challenges include the early preclinical stage of evidence, absence of human clinical data in gonorrhea, and the need to confirm safety, effective dosing, and pharmacodynamic activity in urogenital tissues. As acetazolamide is systemically active and used for other indications, evaluation of appropriate dosing regimens and potential off-target effects in the context of infectious disease will be necessary. Additionally, resistance development and compatibility with existing dual-therapy strategies require further study.
Overall, acetazolamide represents a repurposed agent with promising preclinical anti-gonococcal activity through a novel enzymatic target. Advancement into clinical studies will be essential to determine its feasibility and positioning within the gonorrhea treatment landscape.

Name: Adiponectin/leptin ratio
Developers: University of Tehran; University of Tehran
Indication: Diagnosis of metabolic dysfunction, insulin resistance, and increased cardiovascular risk
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Mechanism of action: Calculates adiponectin-to-leptin ratio to assess adipose dysfunction and insulin resistance associated with PCOS.
Key features and challenges:
The adiponectin/leptin (A/L) ratio has emerged as a potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarker in various metabolic and inflammatory conditions. Both adiponectin and leptin are adipokines secreted by adipose tissue, playing critical roles in metabolic homeostasis. The A/L ratio reflects the balance between the beneficial (adiponectin) and detrimental (leptin) effects of adipose tissue function. A Low A/L ratio indicates metabolic dysfunction, insulin resistance, and increased cardiovascular risk.

A review study published in 2023 evaluates the adiponectin-to-leptin (A:L) ratio as a potential biomarker for PCOS. A meta-analysis of nine studies demonstrated a significantly lower A:L ratio in women with PCOS compared to controls, with a standardized mean difference of 0.49 (CI: 0.37–0.61), indicating a consistent association. No significant heterogeneity or publication bias was observed. These findings suggest that the A:L ratio could serve as a promising biomarker, offering new insights into the pathophysiology and diagnosis of PCOS. (https://www.rbmojournal.com/article/S1472-6483(23)00653-3/abstract)

Another study published in 2023 assessed the adiponectin/leptin (A/L) and HOMA/adiponectin (H/A) ratios in 150 Iranian women with PCOS (60 infertile, 90 with recurrent pregnancy loss) and 50 non-PCOS controls. Results showed a decreased A/L ratio and an increased H/A ratio in PCOS women, both strongly associated with PCOS, regardless of infertility or RPL status. ROC curve analysis demonstrated high predictive accuracy for PCOS, with AUCs of 0.867 (A/L) and 0.861 (H/A). While these ratios are reliable markers for PCOS, they are less effective in distinguishing between infertility and RPL within PCOS. (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11845-023-03408-4)

Name: Adult Oviposition and Larvicidal Ovitrap (ALO)

Indication: Prevention and control of Aedes mosquito-borne arboviral diseases
