Preterm labour is a secondary outcome measure.

Name: Pre-Twin Screen - PE
Developers: University of Bonn, Universitaet Bonn; University of Tubingen (including the Natural and Medical Sciences Institute, NMI); King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust; Yitzhak Shamir University; McGill University (including The Royal Institution for the Advancement of Learning)
Indication: Detection of preeclampsia in twin pregnancies
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Target: Prior risk, biochemical, endocrine, imagine, immunology and cell free DNA (cfDNA) measures
Mechanism of action: Combines maternal biomarkers, Doppler indices, and clinical factors to estimate individualized risk of preeclampsia in twin pregnancies.
Key features and challenges:
The prevalence of twin pregnancies is rising globally due to increased assisted conception and advanced maternal age in pregnancy. Twin pregnancies have 5-9 times higher frequencies of fetal chromosomal and structural abnormalities, often deliver preterm, and have high prevalence of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), preeclampsia (PE), and intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) compared to singletons. 

The Pre-Twin Screen project aim to develop a multi-marker, personalized, prenatal diagnostics model to predict feto-maternal complications in twins. A multi-national network will recruit a statistically powered cohort of 1,200 twins and follow them through pregnancy up to delivery utilizing prior risk, biochemical, endocrine, imaging, immunology and cell free DNA (cfDNA) measures. Initial twin cohorts revealed good prediction of Down syndrome, PE, and GDM by prior risk, ultrasound and serum markers. The study will test all the above, add cfDNA and evaluate structural and chromosomal abnormalities, imaging standardised for MC twins, and endocrine, sonographic, and biophysical markers. 
The markers investigated include imaging (chorionicity, placental location, Vasa Previa, TTTS, Doppler blood flow to internal fetal organs including Ductus Venousus, biochemical markers (PAPP-A, PlGF, PP13, Inhibin A, HCG), biophysical measures (mean arterial blood pressure (MAP), UTPI), and immunological markers of white blood cells (mainly natural killer cell (NK cells).
(https://clinmedjournals.org/articles/ijwhw/international-journal-of-womens-health-and-wellness-ijwhw-6-110.php?jid=ijwhw)

Latest 2025 publications: (https://obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/pd.6820) (https://karger.com/fdt/article/doi/10.1159/000546981/931151/Third-Trimester-Screening-for-Preeclampsia-in) (https://cdn.fortunejournals.com/articles/fetal-growth-chart-in-twins-consistent-with-the-fmf-growth-curve-prospective-multicenter-study.pdf)

Name: PreEclampsia Predictor with Machine Learning (PEPrML)
Developers: Columbia University
Indication: Prediction of severe preeclampsia and eclampsia
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Target: Blood pressure, uterine artery blood flow, placental analytes, Endoglin, Cholesterol, and Inhibin A
Mechanism of action: Quantifies urinary androgen metabolites to estimate androgen exposure and identify hyperandrogenism consistent with PCOS.
Key features and challenges:
​Researchers at Columbia University developed screening models for the prediction of preeclampsia through machine learning, using the prospective Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-to-be (nuMoM2b) study, with maternal serum samples collected for 1,857 individuals between the first and second trimesters. 
 
The study aimed to build bias-free machine learning classifiers at various discrete points in pregnancy that combine well-known risk factors for and indicators of severe preeclampsia and eclampsia, which can help screen for cases early in pregnancy in a nulliparous study cohort. Because of the importance of obstetric history in several predictive models, there is a need for nulliparous specific predictive models where predictive ability is not dependant on previous pregnancies. The study focuses on most severe cases so those with mild preeclampsia, superimposed preeclampsia, and new onset hypertension were excluded. 
 
The Preeclampsia Predictor with Machine Learning (PEPrML) model is based on the following identified predictive features: blood pressure, uterine artery blood flow, placental analytes, endoglin, cholesterol, and Inhibin A. Classifiers to predict severe preeclampsia or eclampsia versus no pregnancy-related hypertension and early severe preeclampsia versus late severe preeclampsia or eclampsia were modelled for 3 different antenatal visit points: the first between 6 and 13 weeks of gestation (V1), the second between 16 and 21 weeks of gestation (V2), and the third between 22 and 29 weeks of gestation (V3). For the prediction of preeclampsia/eclampsia versus no pregnancy-related hypertension, the models achieved an AUC of 0.72 at V1, 0.75 at V2, and 0.77 at V3. For the prediction of early severe preeclampsia versus late severe preeclampsia/eclampsia, RF models obtained an AUC of 0.64 at V1, 0.76 at V2, and 0.83 at V3 (https://bmcpregnancychildbirth.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12884-024-06988-w).

Name: PrePsia
Developers: Metabolomic Diagnostics Ltd
Indication: Diagnosis and prediction of PE
Health care facility level: IVDs for Primary health care
Mechanism of action: Contains antimicrobial peptides that disrupt bacterial membranes and inhibit growth of Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
Key features and challenges:
​PrePsia is a biomarker test currently being developed by Metabolomic Diagnostics. 
 
The EU-funded IPOG project ("Improving Pregnancy Outcomes Globally") analysed thousands of blood samples from pregnant women by mass spectrometry to identify preeclampsia-associated biomarkers. 
(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24314209/ and (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/822842).  
 
The test would combine PlGF testing and single metabolites (including  2-hydroxy-(2/3)-methylbutyric acid, 25-hydroxyvitamin D3, 2-hydroxybutyric acid, alanine, dodecanoylcarnitine, and 1-(1Z-octadecenyl)-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine) and ratios of amino acids related to arginine bioavailability and nitric oxide synthase pathways according to a scientific article published on the project's website (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0002937822022906?dgcid=coauthor). The test could be conducted at 11-13 weeks of gestation. 
 
Additional information: (https://cordis.europa.eu/docs/results/305/305169/final1-improved-305169-final-report-section1.pdf).

Name: PreTeL’s Labor Status Monitor
Developers: PRETEL, INC.
Indication: EMG device to diagnose true and false labour for women with threatened preterm labour.
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Mechanism of action: The core technology (uterine EMG) is combined with directional EMG sensors, called Area Sensors, which are used to localize signals originating on the uterine wall. Then local contractions are analyzed based on the degree of synchronization or timing of the signals at different locations on the uterus. The Area Sensors reveal a unique EMG signal between contractions and characterize False Labor from True Labor.
Key features and challenges:
PreTeL is developing the Labor Status Monitor, an investigational device designed to differentiate true labour from false labour in women presenting with threatened preterm labour. The platform is based on a proprietary “Area Sensor” technology that measures regional uterine electrical synchronisation using electromyography (EMG), combined with fetal and maternal electrocardiography (ECG) monitoring. The system aims to provide real-time assessment of contraction type, synchronisation patterns, and progression of labour.
In 2016, prior research validated mechanotransduction processes in the myometrium, supporting the physiological basis for evaluating uterine electrical activity to characterise contraction strength and coordination.
(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27165050/)
A clinical study (NCT03785795) enrolled 23 participants to observe uterine bioelectrical signals using PreTeL’s directional EMG “area sensor,” which is designed to preferentially detect contractions originating beneath the sensor location. This approach enables non-invasive evaluation of uterine synchronisation and contraction strength in real time.
(https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03785795)
In 2023, further studies reported validation of this methodology for clinical interpretation of uterine contractions and synchronisation patterns in labour assessment.
(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37217825/)
(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37164493/)
The device currently requires approximately one hour of monitoring for evaluation, with future development aimed at reducing assessment time. The system is not yet commercially available and is seeking U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval. In 2023, PreTeL announced enrolment of the first patients in an NIH SBIR-supported study evaluating the Labor Status Monitor for diagnosing true versus false labour in preterm patients.
(https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10484554)
(https://pretelhealth.com/)
Overall, the PreTeL Labor Status Monitor represents an investigational, electrophysiology-based diagnostic tool aimed at improving discrimination between true and false labour and enhancing management of threatened preterm labour. Further clinical validation and regulatory review are required prior to routine clinical implementation.

Name: Preaxinellamine
Developers: King Saud University (KSU, formerly Riyadh University)
Indication: Treatment of gonorrhoea
Mechanism of action: Marine-derived alkaloid exhibiting antibacterial activity through disruption of essential bacterial cellular processes.
Key features and challenges: Preclinical study was published in 2023 investigating the molecular interactions of three PBP2 variants with halogenated marine sponge metabolites using molecular docking, molecular dynamic simulation, and ADMET analysis. The docking findings were evaluated using the glide gscore, and the top 20 compounds docked against each PBP2 protein receptor were chosen. Furthermore, the selected compounds underwent ADMET analysis, indicating that they have the potential for therapeutic development. Among the selected compounds Preaxinellamine had the highest affinity for the cephalosporin-resistant variant of PBP2 protein. The results of the study suggest that these compounds may eventually be used to treat gonorrhoea. However, computer validations were included in this study, and more in-vitro research is required to turn these prospective inhibitors into clinical drugs. (https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/07391102.2023.2292291)
Recent updates: Molecular docking and ADMET studies were published in 2023 (https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/07391102.2023.2292291).

Name: PrediMAP in-vitro diagnostic medical device
Developers: Assistance Publique - Hôpitaux de Paris
Indication: A test combining clinical and ultrasound data with biomarkers to construct an algorithm to predict PTB within 7 days after the test.
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Target: ultrasound data, biomarkers in vaginal samples
Mechanism of action: Collection of vaginal samples for the development of the device, clinical and ultrasound data for the predictive algorithm, and placenta and membrane samples to identify additional biomarkers (not determined at this time).
Key features and challenges:
PrediMAP is an investigational in-vitro diagnostic (IVD) device designed to predict delivery within seven days among women presenting to obstetric emergency services with symptoms of preterm labour. The platform integrates clinical parameters, ultrasound findings, and biomarker data into a predictive algorithm intended to stratify short-term preterm birth risk.
A clinical trial initiated in 2022 and running through 2027 is establishing a prospective cohort to support development and validation of the device. The study involves collection of vaginal samples for biomarker discovery, clinical and ultrasound data for algorithm construction, and placental and membrane samples to identify additional predictive markers. Results have not yet been reported, and the specific biomarkers incorporated into the algorithm have not been publicly disclosed.
(https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05586334)
Overall, PrediMAP represents a multi-modal predictive approach combining biological and clinical data to estimate imminent preterm delivery risk. Clinical validation data are pending, and the device remains under development.
Recent updates: Current clinical trial, enrolling 2022-2027.

Name: Predictive model: cervico-vaginal cytokines, cervical length and maternal age
Developers: Instituto Nacional de Perinatología Isidro Espinosa de los Reyes,; Universidad Autónoma Metropolitana
Indication: Prediction of PTL
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Target: cytokines in cervical-vaginal mucus (IL-2, IL-6, IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-10, IL-1ra ), cervical length, maternal age
Mechanism of action: Ultrasound assessment of stromal echogenicity to identify increased stromal volume and fibrosis characteristic of polycystic ovaries.
Key features and challenges:
A cytokine-mediated inflammatory process is known to be involved in the pathophysiology of preterm birth.  Researchers from the Instituto Nacional de Perinatología Isidro Espinosa de los Reyes, Mexico, quantified cytokines in cervical-vaginal mucus of pregnant women (18–23.6 weeks of gestation) with high or low risk for preterm birth determined by cervical length, also collecting relevant obstetric information. IL-2, IL-6, IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-10 were significantly higher in the high-risk group, while IL-1ra was lower. Two different models for preterm birth prediction were created using the Random Forest machine-learning algorithm: a full model with 12 clinical variables and cytokine values and the adjusted model, including the most relevant variables-maternal age, IL-2, and cervical length- (detection rate 66 vs. 87%, false positive rate 12 vs. 3.33%, false negative rate 28 vs. 6.66%, and area under the curve 0.722 vs. 0.875, respectively). The adjusted model that incorporate cytokines showed a detection rate eight points higher than the gold standard calculator, which may allow us to identify the risk PB risk more accurately and implement strategies for preventive interventions.
(https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/24/18/13851)

Name: Prednisolone - PTL/PTB
Developers: University of Mostar
Indication: For the prevention of preterm labour
Mechanism of action: Corticosteroid Hormone Receptor Agonist
Key features and challenges:
Prednisolone is a glucocorticoid that is prednisone in which the oxo group at position 11 has been reduced to the corresponding beta-hydroxy group. It is a drug metabolite of prednisone. It has a role as an adrenergic agent, an anti-inflammatory drug, an antineoplastic agent, an immunosuppressive agent, a drug metabolite, an environmental contaminant and a xenobiotic. 
The effect of low doses of intermediate acting corticosteroids on the prolongation of pregnancy in threatened preterm birth has not yet been studied. Given that PTB is a syndrome characterized by a strong inflammatory response, researchers hypothesize that low doses of an intermediate acting CS for 3 weeks after tocolysis and RDS prophylaxis may help prolong singleton pregnancy in women with threatening PTB, without harmful consequences for mother and child.
A clinical trial which started in 2023 is testing the effect of low dose of prednisone (5mg) in prevention of preterm labour in single pregnancies. Study participants are singleton pregnancies in 24th until 34th week of gestation with a sign of threatening preterm birth at the time of admission: uterine contractions more than 4 in 20 minutes or more than 8 in 60 minutes with concomitant bleeding accompanied by cervical dilation more than 2 cm, cervical effacement less than 20 mm using transvaginal probe, progression in gynecological findings at the time of admission. The study is expected to be completed in 2025. 
(https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06103227)

Name: Preeclampsia Screening Test - Intignus Biotech
Developers: Intignus Biotech
Indication: Prediction of risk of developing preeclampsia
Health care facility level: IVDs for Primary health care
Mechanism of action: Detects protein from a drop of sample in 15-20 minutes
Key features and challenges:
The Intignus Biotech Preeclampsia Screening Test is a rapid, point-of-care lateral flow assay designed for early detection of preeclampsia risk. The device requires two drops of capillary blood and provides results within approximately 15 minutes. Similar in format to other rapid diagnostic strip tests, the assay displays one, two, or three lines corresponding to risk stratification categories: one line indicates low risk, two lines indicate low-to-moderate risk, and three lines indicate high risk or imminent symptom development. The test is based on detection of a placental-origin receptor biomarker associated with preeclampsia pathophysiology.
The screening kit is designed to be low cost, instrument-free, and operable by minimally trained personnel, supporting potential use in low-resource settings. The manufacturer indicates that the test may detect risk of preeclampsia before 16 weeks’ gestation, positioning it as an early screening tool rather than a diagnostic confirmation assay 
(https://intignusbiotech.com/preeclampsia-screening-test/).
Key challenges include limited publicly available peer-reviewed validation data, unclear diagnostic performance metrics (e.g., sensitivity, specificity, predictive values), and need for external clinical validation across diverse populations and gestational ages. Regulatory status and integration into established screening algorithms will be critical factors in determining clinical adoption and scale-up potential.

Name: Preptin
Developers: University of Baghdad; Kayseri City Education and Research Hospital
Indication: Diagnosis of PCOS and assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR)
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Mechanism of action: ELISA
Key features and challenges:
Preptin is an oligopeptide co-secreted with insulin by pancreatic β-cells and has been investigated as a potential biomarker for polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), particularly due to its role in glucose-mediated insulin secretion.
A 2021 study involving 100 Iraqi women (50 with PCOS and 50 controls) reported significantly higher levels of prolactin, luteinizing hormone (LH), preptin, and CCL18 in women with PCOS. Testosterone and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) were also elevated in the PCOS group, suggesting that preptin may serve as a potential biomarker associated with the disorder.
(Source: https://www.bsj.uobaghdad.edu.iq/index.php/BSJ/article/view/6125)
A 2022 study examining infertile women with PCOS found significantly higher serum levels of anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), preptin, insulin, and testosterone compared to controls. A positive correlation between preptin and AMH was identified, suggesting a potential metabolic and reproductive link that warrants further investigation.
(Source: https://journals.indexcopernicus.com/api/file/viewByFileId/1543712)
A 2023 meta-analysis of eight studies comprising 582 participants demonstrated significantly elevated serum preptin levels in women with PCOS compared to control groups (standardized mean difference [SMD] = 1.35; 95% CI: 0.63–2.08; p < 0.001). Subgroup analysis indicated that preptin levels were particularly elevated among women with higher insulin resistance (HOMA-IR > 3), supporting a potential association between preptin and metabolic dysfunction in PCOS.
(Source: https://kneopen.com/ijrm/article/view/13470/)
Overall, available evidence suggests that preptin may serve as a biomarker reflecting metabolic disturbances in PCOS, particularly in individuals with insulin resistance. However, associations with age and BMI appear inconsistent, indicating that its diagnostic utility may be context-dependent and require further validation in larger, well-controlled studies.

Name: Primaquine
Developers: University of California, San Francisco (UCSF)
Indication: Indicated for the treatment of Endometriosis.
Target: Under investigation - likely involves gene expression and/or pain signalling.
Mechanism of action: Under investigation.
Key features and challenges:
Primaquine is an 8-aminoquinoline antimalarial agent traditionally used for radical cure of Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale infections. Although primarily developed for infectious diseases, its immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory properties have prompted investigation into potential repurposing applications. Endometriosis is characterized by chronic inflammation, altered immune signaling, and dysregulated gene expression, making computational drug repositioning a promising strategy for identifying novel therapeutics.
A 2025 preclinical study evaluated primaquine alongside simvastatin using a computational screening approach based on gene expression reversal scores (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.05.28.656743v1). 
Of 299 drugs identified through transcriptomic analysis, primaquine ranked highly for reversing endometriosis-associated gene expression signatures. In vivo validation was conducted using a rat model of endometriosis-associated pain. Behavioral testing demonstrated that primaquine significantly reduced vaginal hyperalgesia, a surrogate marker of endometriosis-related pain. Bulk RNA sequencing of uterine tissue and ectopic lesions confirmed that primaquine treatment reversed disease-associated transcriptional changes.
These findings suggest that primaquine may attenuate pain behaviors and modulate pathogenic molecular pathways in endometriosis, supporting its potential as a repurposed non-hormonal therapeutic candidate.
Key challenges include the exclusively preclinical nature of the evidence and lack of human clinical trial data. Primaquine is associated with known risks, including hemolytic anemia in individuals with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, which would necessitate screening and monitoring in reproductive-age populations. Its safety profile in long-term use for non-infectious indications remains unclear. Further mechanistic studies and well-designed clinical trials are required to evaluate efficacy, optimal dosing, and safety in women with endometriosis.

Name: ProC6C-Alhydrogel/Matrix-M
Developers: University of Bamako (including University of Science, Techniques and Technology Bamako (USTTB) and WANECAM); University of Oxford (including Oxford University Clinical Research Unit Vietnam (OUCRU), Nuffield Department of Women's and Reproductive Health (NDWRH)); Statens Serum Institute (SSI)
Indication: Indicated for active immunization against malaria caused by P.falciparum

Name: Probe fluorescence RT- PCR assay
Developers: Smolensk State Medical University
Indication: Detection of Mycoplasma genitalium and antimicrobial susceptibility
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Mechanism of action: 23S rRNA gene mutation detection
Key features and challenges:
Probe fluorescence RT-PCR assay is a real-time molecular diagnostic developed to detect macrolide resistance–associated mutations in the 23S rRNA gene of Mycoplasma genitalium. The assay utilizes probe fluorescence quenching by a primer and melting curve analysis to identify nucleotide substitutions at positions 2058, 2059, and 2611 (Escherichia coli numbering) immediately following amplification.
A 2023 study validated the assay and reported 92% sensitivity and 100% specificity for detection of macrolide resistance mutations in clinical and spiked samples (https://www.liebertpub.com/doi/10.1089/mdr.2022.0131). 
The assay was applied to 949 nonduplicate urogenital specimens collected between 2009 and 2019 from symptomatic patients in five cities in European Russia, enabling assessment of resistance prevalence in a large clinical cohort.
Key challenges include incomplete sensitivity for mutation detection, potential emergence of novel resistance-associated variants not covered by the assay, and the need for validation across broader geographic and epidemiological settings. Integration into routine workflows and cost considerations may also affect uptake.
Overall, the probe fluorescence RT-PCR assay offers a genotype-based approach for rapid detection of macrolide-resistant M. genitalium. Expanded validation and surveillance integration are required to support routine clinical implementation.

Name: Probenecid
Developers: University of Georgia (UGA) (including the Center for Vaccines and Immunology); Georgia Research Alliance
Indication: Treatment of influenza A, caused by H5N1
Target: Host organic anion transporter 3 (OAT3) and JNK/MAPK signaling pathways
Mechanism of action: Inhibits OAT3 and JNK phosphorylation, disrupting host cell pathways essential for influenza virus replication. This blocks viral replication and reduces pro-inflammatory cytokine release (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β).
Key features and challenges:
-FDA-approved for gout since 1951; long safety record.
-Exhibits broad-spectrum antiviral effects (influenza, RSV, SARS-CoV-2).
-Potent in vitro and in vivo efficacy against H5N1 and H7N9; superior to oseltamivir in some assays.
-Dual benefit: antiviral + anti-inflammatory effects.
-Challenge: Requires repurposing and clinical trials for influenza; pharmacokinetics/dosing optimization needed for respiratory infections.
Recent updates:
2024:
-Demonstrated IC50 values in nanomolar range for H5N1 and H7N9 in human lung cells.
-In mice, 100 mg/kg probenecid eliminated H5N1 lung virus titers and improved survival compared to oseltamivir.
-Phase 2 trial in COVID-19 showed shortened viral clearance and improved symptom resolution, supporting potential for influenza clinical testing.
-Investigated for its ability to inhibit PANX1 signaling and reduce hyperinflammation, strengthening its role in severe influenza pathology.

Name: Probiotic Bio-three
Developers: University of Toyama Hospital; Toa Biopharma
Indication: Preventing Spontaneous Preterm Birth
Mechanism of action: Unknown
Key features and challenges:
Bio-three is a probiotic combination formulation containing three bacterial strains: Enterococcus faecalis T-110, Clostridium butyricum TO-A, and Bacillus mesentericus TO-A. The product is marketed as an oral dispersible (OD) tablet and is intended to promote intestinal microbial balance. Probiotics have been investigated for their potential role in modulating inflammation and immune responses during pregnancy, given the proposed association between dysbiosis, inflammation, and spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB).
In 2021, a multicenter, open-label clinical study was initiated to evaluate whether probiotic supplementation beginning in the first trimester could reduce recurrent spontaneous preterm birth in women with a prior history of sPTB. The trial utilizes TOA Biopharma’s Bio-three combination OD tablets (6 tablets; 3 g total daily dose). Results from this study have not yet been published.
(https://jrct.niph.go.jp/en-latest-detail/jRCTs041210014)
Overall, Bio-three represents an investigational probiotic approach aimed at reducing recurrent spontaneous preterm birth through microbiome modulation. Clinical efficacy and safety data specific to PTL/PTB prevention remain pending.

Name: Probiotic Lactobacilli - PTL/PTB
Developers: The Madras Medical Mission Hospital; National Maternity Hospital Ireland
Indication: Reducing risk of preterm birth due to vaginosis
Mechanism of action: Modulating pH and constituents of vaginal microbiome to prevent vaginosis
Key features and challenges:
Lactobacilli form an integral part of the vaginal microbiota. They help to maintain the pH of the vaginal tract and provide effective immunity to the host by producing lactic acid and hydrogen peroxide. The presence of abnormal vaginal microbiota in the early stages of pregnancy is a risk factor for preterm birth. Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is an important and independent risk factor for preterm birth. It is characterized by a reduction of beneficial Lactobacilli and heavy colonization of anaerobic bacteria. Pathogens ascending through vagina and cervix to uterus release bacterial proteolytic enzymes like phospholipase A2 and collagenase. This initiates the formation of arachidonic acid and increases the level of prostaglandins. Elevated prostaglandin levels induce collagen remodelling in the foetal membranes. This will eventually lead to uterine contraction and preterm labour. Among many strains of Lactobacilli, Lactobacillus rhamnosus GR1 and Lactobacillus reuteri RC14 are found to have excellent colonizing capability and are the preferred Lactobacilli strain for the treatment of urogenital tract infections.  

BV also increases the risk of PTB is through endotoxins secreted by pathogens, such as lipopolysaccharides (LPSs), potentially leading to LPS-induced preterm labour. Once BV is diagnosed in pregnancy, antibiotics are the first-line treatment, despite studies demonstrating no correlation between antibiotic treatment and delaying of labour. Some studies have posited that that while antibacterial treatment does combat pathogens, it neglects replenishment of commensal microbiota which protect against infection, resulting in a lack of protection and subsequent reinfection.

Several studies have proved Lactobacilli to have beneficial perinatal outcome on prenatal administration, likely due to replenishment of beneficial lactobacilli. The available data in medical literature shows that Lactobacillus rhamnosus GR1 and Lactobacillus reuteri RC14 are beneficial and safe for use in pregnancy to prevent preterm labour, if administered at or before 20 weeks of gestational age (reviewed in: https://www.jcgo.org/index.php/jcgo/article/view/571/371). A 2002 study showed that the absence of lactobacilli was a better predictor of preterm delivery at < 33 weeks of gestation than the presence of other bacteria (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12530101/). However, a 2018 Cochrane Review found insufficient evidence to conclude any benefits to for prevention of morbidity or mortality of preterm infants (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30548483/).

The National Maternity Hospital (Ireland) and the UCD Perinatal Research Centre (Ireland) started a research study in 2020 to identify whether providing healthy microbes in an oral probiotic supplement during pregnancy improves vaginal health and reduces preterm birth in women at high risk of having a preterm baby. This randomized controlled trial investigating the impact of oral probiotic supplementation on the microbiome in pregnant women at high risk of preterm birth is due to be completed in 2026 (https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN11963471).
 
A 2021 Iranian study is evaluating the use of the probiotic, Lactofem, on prevention of preterm delivery in mothers at risk of preterm delivery. The Lactofem capsules used for research contains live strains of lactobacilli. Different formulations have been produced by Iranian zist-takhmir Company for research (A: Oral probiotic (500 mg lactofem capsule, which contained Lactobacillus probiotic strains[L.acidophilus(5 × 1010CFU/g), L.plantarum(1.5 × 1010 CFU/g), L.fermentum(7 × 109CFU/g) and L.Gasseri (2 × 1010CFU/g)]) and (B: Lactofem capsule, including Lactobacillus acidophilus 2 × 109 cfu/g, Bifidobacterium bifidus 2 × 109 cfu/g, Lactobacillus rutri 2 × 109 cfu/g, Lactobacillus fermentum 2 × 109 cfu/g; capsule weight of 500 mg bio-capsule). (https://irct.behdasht.gov.ir/trial/58571)
(https://www.medicinesfaq.com/brand/lactofem)

Name: Progesterone - PCOS
Developers: Nazarbayev University
Indication: Diagnosis of PCOS
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Mechanism of action: Measures luteal-phase progesterone to assess ovulatory function and detect anovulation associated with PCOS.
Key features and challenges:
Progesterone, a hormone produced by the ovaries after ovulation, is often low in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) due to frequent anovulation. This imbalance contributes to irregular periods, infertility, and risks like endometrial hyperplasia.

In diagnostics, mid-luteal phase progesterone levels (<3 ng/mL) indicate anovulation, a key PCOS feature. Measuring progesterone helps differentiate PCOS from other menstrual disorders and predict fertility outcomes. However, its variability limits its standalone diagnostic value, prompting research into integrated hormonal assessments. A 2022 study found that women with PCOS had significantly lower serum progesterone levels compared to those without the condition, suggesting that reduced progesterone could serve as a diagnostic marker for PCOS. (https://www.mdpi.com/2227-9059/12/10/2333)

Name: Progesterone, natural, micronized (oral) - PTL/PTB
Developers: AbbVie; Besins Healthcare; Virtus Pharmaceuticals
Indication: Reducing risk of preterm labour in women with history of preterm birth or women with short cervix
Mechanism of action: Progesterone reduces risk of subsequent preterm delivery by modulating levels of HLA-G, which is linked to spontaneous preterm birth and intra-amniotic inflammation or infections.
Key features and challenges:
Progesterone (natural, micronized; oral) is a naturally occurring steroid hormone (progestogen) used in a range of reproductive health indications, including luteal support in pregnancy and fertility care, and in combination with oestrogens for menopausal hormone therapy. Owing to its immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects, progesterone has been investigated for prevention of preterm labour/birth (PTL/PTB) in women at elevated risk. Progesterone has also been reported to increase placental HLA-G production in cytotrophoblast cells, a pathway implicated in spontaneous preterm birth and intra-amniotic inflammation or infection.
A 2013 Cochrane review evaluated progestogens for women at risk of preterm birth due to a prior spontaneous PTB or short cervix.
(https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23903965/). 
In women with a previous preterm birth, progestogens reduced the risk of PTB before 34 weeks and were associated with reductions in perinatal mortality, low birthweight, and neonatal death. In women with cervical shortening, the main consistent benefit was a reduction in PTB before 34 weeks, while effects on other outcomes were not statistically significant. The review reported no clear differential effects by route of administration, timing of initiation, or dose for most outcomes.
A 2019 meta-analysis specifically assessing oral progesterone concluded that oral progesterone appears effective in preventing recurrent PTB and reducing perinatal morbidity and mortality in asymptomatic singleton pregnancies with a history of spontaneous PTB, compared with placebo (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31172132/). 
Adverse effects were more frequent with oral progesterone than placebo, although none were reported as serious. In contrast, a 2022 comparative study from India reported that vaginal micronized progesterone was more effective than oral micronized progesterone in reducing preterm labour and improving neonatal outcomes, including lower NICU admission rates and reduced neonatal morbidity and mortality (https://www.academia.edu/117685971/Comparative_study_of_oral_and_vaginal_natural_micronized_progesterone_300mg_in_preventing_preterm_labor_in_semi_urban_population).
Key challenges include variability in demonstrated benefit by risk subgroup, uncertainty regarding optimal route of administration for specific populations, and tolerability considerations for oral formulations. While evidence supports a preventive role for progestogens in selected high-risk pregnancies, further high-quality comparative trials are needed to clarify where oral micronized progesterone provides the greatest clinical value relative to vaginal formulations and other PTB prevention strategies.
Recent updates:
2019: Oral progesterone for the prevention of recurrent preterm birth: systematic review and metaanalysis. (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31172132/)

A 2020 Cochrane review found that for women with cervical shortening, among the above outcomes, only preterm birth before 34 weeks was reduced by progestogen. 

2022: Clinical trial comparing oral and vaginal natural micronized progesterone in preventing preterm labour in India demonstrated vaginal micronized progesterone helps in reduction of preterm labor and the rate of neonatal NICU admissions, neonatal mortality and morbidity as compared to oral micronized progesterone (https://www.academia.edu/117685971/Comparative_study_of_oral_and_vaginal_natural_micronized_progesterone_300mg_in_preventing_preterm_labor_in_semi_urban_population)

Name: Progestin vaginal ring - VR 103
Developers: VaRi Bioscience
Indication: Treatment of endometriosis pain, menorrhagia and lesions
Mechanism of action: Progesterone receptor agonists
Key features and challenges:
VR 103 is a non-invasive vaginal ring developed by VaRi Bioscience for long-acting progestin therapy in endometriosis. Progestin therapy is an established hormonal strategy in endometriosis, associated with reduction in pain symptoms and suppression of lesion activity (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10127994/). 
VR 103 utilizes proprietary polymer technology designed to provide sustained, controlled release of progestin over approximately three months, with potential platform applicability ranging from one month to five years (https://vari-bioscience.com/pipeline/).
Unlike GnRH agonists and antagonists, which induce hypoestrogenic states, VR 103 is intended to deliver therapeutic progestin exposure while maintaining plasma estrogen levels within a range that minimizes estrogen withdrawal symptoms and mitigates bone mineral density loss. This approach aims to combine efficacy in pain and lesion control with improved tolerability.
As of February 2023, VR 103 is undergoing a Phase IIa clinical trial in Germany for the treatment of endometriosis (https://adis.springer.com/drugs/800072438). 
Preliminary safety findings indicate that the device does not significantly suppress plasma estrogen concentrations, suggesting a potentially favorable bone safety profile. Early data also suggest good tolerability compared with other progestin-only therapies, with limited estrogen withdrawal–related adverse effects. Detailed efficacy outcomes remain limited in the public domain.
Key challenges include the need to demonstrate robust, clinically meaningful pain reduction and lesion control in controlled trials, as well as confirmation of long-term safety and continuation rates. Market positioning will depend on differentiation from existing oral and intrauterine progestin therapies, particularly regarding bleeding patterns, adherence, and quality-of-life outcomes.
Overall, VR 103 represents a long-acting, locally delivered progestin approach aiming to balance efficacy with improved tolerability in endometriosis. Confirmation of clinical benefit and long-term safety in Phase II/III studies will be critical to define its therapeutic role.

Name: Prolactin - PCOS
Developers: Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research (including Sri Ramachandra Hospital)
Indication: Diagnosis of PCOS
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Mechanism of action: Measures serum prolactin to detect hyperprolactinemia contributing to menstrual irregularities and PCOS-like endocrine features.
Key features and challenges:
Prolactin is a hormone primarily produced by the anterior pituitary gland, with smaller amounts secreted by the immune system, the uterus, and the placenta. Its main function is to stimulate milk production after childbirth. In addition to its role in reproduction, prolactin influences a variety of biological processes including reproductive health, immune function and metabolic regulation. 

A study published in 2022 investigated the association between obesity, serum prolactin, and insulin levels in women with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). Conducted on 30 PCOS patients and 30 healthy controls aged 20-40 years, the study measured serum prolactin and insulin using ELISA. Results showed significantly higher insulin levels in PCOS patients, with a cutoff value of 7.0 mIU/L, indicating insulin resistance. Prolactin levels were also elevated, correlating with BMI and age. The study concluded that insulin resistance and hyperprolactinemia are prevalent in obese PCOS women, suggesting that prolactin and insulin may serve as potential diagnostic markers for the condition. (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366806828_Association_of_prolactin_and_insulin_with_obesity_in_women_with_polycystic_ovarian_syndrome)

Name: Prolyl tRNA synthetase (ProRS) inhibitors

L35 exhibits the highest potency of ∼1.6 nM against asexual-blood-stage (ABS) and ∼100-fold (effective concentration [EC50]) selectivity for the parasite. The macromolecular structures of PfPRS with L95 and L97 in complex with L-pro reveal their binding modes and catalytic site malleability. Name: Promegestone
Developers: Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute; University of Toronto
Indication: Prevent spontaneous preterm birth
Mechanism of action: Selective progesterone receptor modulator
Key features and challenges:
Promegestone is a progestin consisting of 17beta-propionylestra-4,9-dien-3-one substituted at position 17 by a methyl group. It has a role as a progestin, a progesterone receptor agonist and an antineoplastic agent. It is a 3-oxo-Delta(4) steroid and a 20-oxo steroid. It derives from a hydride of an estrane. It binds to progesterone receptors with a higher association constant than progesterone.
It has been hypothesized that promegestone, which is not metabolized by 20α-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, would sustain progesterone receptor signaling and prevent/delay term labor and preterm labor. To test this hypothesis, researchers evaluated the ability of promegestone (PMG) (also known as R5020) to prevent/delay inflammation-induced PTB in a mouse model. 
Promegestone prevented term labor and maintained mice pregnancy post-term >24 hours. The litter size and fetal weights were not different from the controls. Promegestone prevented systemic bacterial-endotoxin-induced preterm labor in 100% of the mice, blocked uterine contractions, significantly inhibited all systemic inflammation-induced myometrial cytokines, and partially inhibited decidual and placental inflammation. Promegestone did not prevent bacterial-endotoxin-induced fetal toxicity. This finding suggests that such selective progesterone receptor modulators may represent a potential therapeutic approach to the prevention of preterm labor in women at high risk of preterm birth.
(https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8810746/)

Name: Promethazine
Developers: Hebrew University of Jerusalem; Magee-Womens Research Institute & Foundation; Kaplan Medical Center
Indication: Indicated for the treatment of Preeclampsia
Target: Histamine H1 Receptors; Mesolimbic Dopamine Receptors & Brainstem Reticular System:
Mechanism of action: Promethazine acts as a competitive, reversible antagonist at H1-receptor sites, which reduces vasodilation and increased capillary permeability
Key features and challenges:
Promethazine is a first-generation antihistamine with established antiemetic and sedative properties and long-standing clinical use in pregnancy for nausea and vomiting. Beyond its H1 receptor antagonism, recent research has identified potential antioxidant and lipid peroxidation–modulating effects, prompting investigation into its role in ferroptosis-related pathways. Ferroptosis, a form of iron-dependent programmed cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has emerged as a potential mechanism contributing to placental dysfunction in preeclampsia (PE), particularly through dysregulation of angiogenic factors such as soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1).
A 2025 study investigated oxidized phosphatidylethanolamines in placental tissues from women with preeclampsia compared with normotensive controls using redox phospholipidomics (https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.125.25003
). Preeclamptic placentas demonstrated significant accumulation of oxidized phosphatidylethanolamines. In placental explants, induction of ferroptosis increased sFlt-1 release, whereas treatment with ferroptosis inhibitors (Ferrostatin-1 and deferoxamine) significantly reduced sFlt-1 levels (P<0.01). A high-throughput screen of 6,520 drugs and compounds identified dipyridamole and promethazine as potent ferroptosis inhibitors in primary trophoblasts. Promethazine reduced lipid peroxidation, preserved glutathione levels, and decreased sFlt-1 release in preeclamptic explants, supporting a potential mechanistic link between ferroptosis inhibition and modulation of angiogenic imbalance in PE.
These findings suggest that placental ferroptosis may contribute to early preeclampsia pathophysiology and that repurposed, approved medications such as promethazine may offer a novel therapeutic strategy targeting oxidative and angiogenic dysregulation.
Key challenges include the in vitro and ex vivo nature of the evidence, with no current in vivo or clinical trial data confirming efficacy in pregnant populations with PE. Optimal dosing for ferroptosis inhibition, maternal–fetal pharmacokinetics, and safety in the context of hypertensive pregnancy disorders remain undefined. Although promethazine has an established obstetric safety record for other indications, its repurposing for PE would require rigorous clinical validation to confirm therapeutic benefit and assess long-term maternal and neonatal outcomes.

Name: Propolis
Developers: Universidade Estadual Paulista (UNESP)
Indication: Preventing the progression of the disease
Mechanism of action: High-sensitivity ultrasound imaging visualizes placental microvascular perfusion to detect reduced blood flow associated with growth restriction.
Key features and challenges:
Propolis, a honeybee product valued for its biological and pharmacological benefits for centuries, has long been used in traditional medicine and, thanks to its antibacterial, antiseptic, anti-inflammatory, and anesthetic properties, in complementary medicine as well. These qualities make it a promising option for managing conditions tied to inflammation and oxidative stress, such as pre-eclampsia. It can help regulate inflammatory responses by lowering levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and damage-associated molecular patterns. In cases like PE, where sterile inflammation is a key factor, these anti-inflammatory effects are especially useful. Propolis reduces cytokine production, often elevated in PE, and also has notable immunomodulatory effects, helping balance the immune system—an important aspect in PE. Rich in antioxidants, it neutralizes free radicals, cutting down oxidative stress and protecting endothelial cells and other tissues from damage, which is crucial for slowing disease progression. However, figuring out the best dosage and way to administer it remains a challenge.

Propolis still needs extensive clinical trials to figure out safe and effective dosing, as current guidelines are unclear. Allergic reactions, especially in people sensitive to bee products, also limit its use. The small amount of clinical data on its safety and effectiveness in humans makes things even trickier. Strong, well-designed trials are essential to prove its benefits. As a natural product, propolis faces tough regulatory hurdles that demand solid evidence of its efficacy and safety. On top of that, possible interactions with other medications need careful consideration, especially for patients taking multiple drugs.

This 2022 study aimed to explore how propolis affects sterile inflammation and endothelial dysfunction by treating monocytes from pre-eclamptic pregnant women and human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) in vitro. The findings could lead to a new therapeutic approach to improve outcomes for both mother and baby. (https://bv.fapesp.br/pt/bolsas/201491/acao-imunomoduladora-da-propolis-sobre-monocitos-de-gestantes-portadoras-de-pre-eclampsia-e-celulas-/)

Name: Propranolol - PPH
Developers: The Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute; Mount Sinai Hospital (Toronto)
Indication: Treatment of PPH
Mechanism of action: Nonselective beta-adrenergic receptor antagonist; Catecholamine production inhibition
Key features and challenges:
Propranolol is a non-selective beta-adrenergic antagonist approved by the FDA in 1967 for cardiovascular and neurological indications including hypertension, angina, arrhythmias, and migraine. Its proposed role in postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) relates to modulation of myometrial responsiveness to oxytocin. Prolonged labour with oxytocin augmentation can lead to desensitisation of oxytocin receptors in the myometrium, increasing the risk of persistent uterine atony and severe PPH. Propranolol is hypothesised to restore or potentiate oxytocin sensitivity by inhibiting β-adrenergic signalling and reducing catecholamine-mediated uterine relaxation.
In 2021, a clinical study investigating propranolol for labour induction reported mixed findings regarding its effectiveness in improving labour outcomes, suggesting that further evaluation of dosing, timing, and patient selection is required. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33421647/
A registered clinical trial is currently investigating propranolol in in vitro studies of naïve and oxytocin-desensitised human myometrium to assess whether propranolol enhances uterine contractility and could reduce the risk of PPH following oxytocin exposure during labour. Study results are not yet available. https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT0343444
Overall, propranolol remains investigational for PPH. Evidence is currently limited to mechanistic and exploratory studies, with no published clinical trials demonstrating clear effectiveness in preventing or treating postpartum haemorrhage.

Name: Propranolol - Uterine fibroids
Developers: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine and Hospital
Indication: Treatment of uterine fibroid tissue growth and angiogenesis
Mechanism of action: Beta 1 adrenergic receptor antagonists
Key features and challenges:
Propranolol hydrochloride is a beta-adrenergic blocker marketed for the treatment of hypertension.
It is being explored for treating uterine fibroids due to its potential anti-angiogenic and anti-proliferative effects. By inhibiting factors like vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), propranolol may reduce blood supply to fibroids, limiting their growth.
(https://go.drugbank.com/drugs/DB00571)

A 2023 nested case-control study was conducted in a population of women aged 18–65 with arterial hypertension. The study investigated propranolol for its anti-angiogenic and anti-proliferative effects on uterine fibroids. Propranolol is thought to inhibit the growth of fibroids by reducing blood flow to the fibroids and inhibiting cell proliferation. The mechanism behind this potential benefit is linked to propranolol’s ability to reduce the expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and other factors involved in the growth and maintenance of fibroids. The study found a significant association of propranolol use with reduced leiomyoma incidence, suggesting that the use of beta-blockers may present a dual benefit of managing hypertension as well as curbing an increased risk of leiomyomas.
(https://www.ejog.org/article/S0301-2115(23)00218-X/abstract)

Name: Proteomic biomarker risk predictor: protein biomarkers and clinical factors
Developers: University of California San Diego School of Medicine
Indication: Prediction of risk of developping preeclampsia
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Target: clinical factors (prior PE, pre-existing hypertension and/or pregestational diabetes mellitus) and serum biomarkers (proteins)
Mechanism of action: Quantifies circulating placental extracellular vesicles to detect altered trophoblast signaling associated with placental dysfunction and preeclampsia.
Key features and challenges: Researchers from UC San Diego conducted a study published in 2022 to develop a predictor of preterm PE (defined as diagnosis with delivery prior to 37 weeks’ GA) that integrates molecular biomarkers and relevant clinical factors into a single risk assessment score that can be used to guide clinical management. Based on the secondary analysis of data from two large mulicentre studies, they developed and validated a predictor of preterm PE across demographically, geographically, and temporally diverse and representative populations integrating a mid-trimester maternal blood-based proteomic signature with established clinical risk factors. They considered 77 biomarker and quality control proteins in maternal serum and three clinical factors (prior PE, pre-existing hypertension and/or pregestational diabetes mellitus), combined into one variable (Clin3), which was deemed positive if any one of the factors were true for the subject. The next step involved testing several classifiers which included no more than one novel two-protein ratio, the one clinical factor variable, and, optionally, the ratio of insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 4 (IBP4) to sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG). Discovery models were ranked by a combination of AUC and correlation with GA at birth amongst preeclamptic subjects, and further filtered for specificity at 75% sensitivity in all women, nulliparous women alone and multiparous women alone, and for significance of contribution of features to the model. They validated nine of these multi-component classifier models, with a predictive performance superior to that of clinical factors alone. Establishing clinical utility for these nine classifiers requires additional research (https://escholarship.org/uc/item/3dd8158g).

Name: Prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC)
Developers: Octapharma
Indication: Treatment and control of postpartum haemorrhage
Mechanism of action: Supplement of prothrombin factors to the coagulation cascade to stop bleeding
Key features and challenges:
Prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC) is a plasma-derived concentrate produced through ion-exchange chromatography of cryoprecipitate supernatant from large plasma pools, following removal of antithrombin and factor XI. Initially developed for the treatment of hemophilia, its use in this setting has declined with the availability of recombinant clotting factor replacements. PCC is currently indicated for the urgent reversal of vitamin K antagonist therapy (e.g., warfarin), reversal of direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC)-associated anticoagulation, and treatment or prophylaxis of bleeding in patients with congenital or acquired deficiencies of vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors (https://go.drugbank.com/drugs/DB11330/
). It is also used perioperatively to reduce bleeding risk in selected patients and in trauma settings requiring massive transfusion. Its potential role has been extended to severe postpartum haemorrhage (PPH), particularly in cases refractory to uterotonics.
PCC differs from fresh frozen plasma (FFP) in that it contains concentrated clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X in an approximate 1:1:1:1 ratio, as well as protein C and protein S. The overall clotting factor concentration is approximately 25-fold higher than that of normal plasma. Small amounts of heparin are included to prevent activation of coagulation factors. Compared with FFP, PCC offers more rapid correction of coagulopathy and requires lower infusion volumes, which may be advantageous in obstetric haemorrhage.
A 2021 clinical trial investigated refinement of PCC use in combination with fibrinogen concentrate for massive obstetric haemorrhage (Patient Blood Management for Massive Obstetric Hemorrhage, NCT03784794: https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03784794
). An earlier study assessing PCC use in postpartum haemorrhage (NCT01910675) was withdrawn in 2018 due to challenges in obtaining informed consent (https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT01910675). 
Current evidence suggests that while PCC may be beneficial in selected cases of severe PPH, its safety profile in obstetric populations requires further evaluation.
Key challenges include the risk of thromboembolic events, particularly when used outside established indications. Evidence specific to obstetric populations remains limited, and optimal dosing strategies in PPH are not fully defined. Regulatory indications do not universally include obstetric haemorrhage, and concerns regarding off-label use and safety monitoring persist. Further high-quality trials are required to clarify efficacy, safety, and appropriate positioning within PPH management algorithms.

Name: Psammaplysin E
Developers: King Saud University (KSU, formerly Riyadh University)
Indication: Treatment of gonorrhoea
Mechanism of action: Natural bromotyrosine compound that inhibits bacterial growth via interference with membrane integrity and metabolic pathways.
Key features and challenges: Preclinical study was published in 2023 investigating the molecular interactions of three PBP2 variants with halogenated marine sponge metabolites using molecular docking, molecular dynamic simulation, and ADMET analysis. The docking findings were evaluated using the glide gscore, and the top 20 compounds docked against each PBP2 protein receptor were chosen. Furthermore, the selected compounds underwent ADMET analysis, indicating that they have the potential for therapeutic development. Among the selected compounds Psammaplysin E had the highest affinity for the penicillin-resistant variation of PBP2 protein. The results of the study suggest that these compounds may eventually be used to treat gonorrhoea. However, computer validations were included in this study, and more in-vitro research is required to turn these prospective inhibitors into clinical drugs. (https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/07391102.2023.2292291)
Recent updates: Molecular docking and ADMET studies were published in 2023 (https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/07391102.2023.2292291).

Name: Pulsatilla Saponin B₄ (PSB₄)
Developers: Guangxi University, Nanning; Jiangxi University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
Indication: Bioactive triterpenoid saponin evaluated for treatment of uterine fibroids using in vivo rat fibroid models, ELISA-based hormone measurements, histopathology, network pharmacology, and molecular docking.
Target:
Key apoptosis- and UF-related proteins identified via docking and network pharmacology:
-BCL-2 (anti-apoptotic)
-BAX (pro-apoptotic)
-Caspase-3 (executioner caspase)
Additional pathway-level targets through KEGG enrichment:
-NF-κB
-MAPK
-IL-17 pathway components
-Lipid/atherosclerosis pathway genes
-Other apoptosis regulators (from in silico analysis)
Mechanism of action:
Pulsatilla saponin B₄ exerts anti-fibroid effects through pro-apoptotic and hormone-lowering mechanisms. In vivo administration (5, 10, 20 mg/kg) significantly restored uterine morphology, reduced uterine weight, normalized smooth-muscle cell arrangement, and decreased inflammatory infiltration. ELISA analyses showed markedly reduced estradiol, progesterone, and estrogen-receptor (ER) levels in serum and uterine tissue.
Network pharmacology revealed 23 PSB₄ targets, with 8 overlapping with leiomyoma-related genes. Pathway analysis indicated involvement of apoptosis, NF-κB, IL-17, MAPK, and lipid/atherosclerosis pathways. Molecular docking confirmed strong binding of PSB₄ to BCL-2, BAX, and Caspase-3, consistent with apoptosis induction.
Western blot validation demonstrated decreased BCL-2 and increased BAX and Caspase-3 protein levels in medium- and high-dose groups, confirming activation of the intrinsic apoptotic pathway.
Overall, PSB₄ acts via hormone down-regulation, ECM modulation, and apoptosis induction, addressing multiple UF pathophysiologic mechanisms.
Key features and challenges:
Pulsatilla saponin B₄ (PSB₄) is a triterpenoid saponin with demonstrated anti-leiomyoma effects in a hormone-induced rat model. Treatment significantly improved uterine morphology, reduced uterine coefficient, normalized cellular arrangement, and reduced inflammatory infiltration. Hormonal assays showed significant reductions in estradiol, progesterone, and estrogen-receptor levels, suggesting modulation of hormone-responsive pathways central to UF growth. Network pharmacology identified 23 compound targets, with 8 overlapping with leiomyoma-associated genes and enrichment across 69 pathways, including apoptosis, IL-17, NF-κB, MAPK, and lipid metabolism. Docking results confirmed high affinity for key apoptotic proteins (BCL-2, BAX, Caspase-3), and Western blotting validated activation of pro-apoptotic signaling (↑BAX, ↑Caspase-3, ↓BCL-2).
Despite strong preclinical evidence, data remains limited to animal models and in silico findings, with no human pharmacokinetic, toxicology, or clinical UF studies. Saponins present challenges related to bioavailability, potential hemolytic effects, batch variability, and scale-up feasibility. Clinical translation would require controlled toxicity studies, formulation optimization, and evaluation of long-term reproductive safety. Nonetheless, PSB₄ demonstrates significant multi-pathway potential as a botanical therapeutic for UF.
Source: https://www.tiprpress.com/ywpjyj/article/abstract/20240703
Recent updates: A 2024 in vivo study confirmed PSB₄’s anti-fibroid effects, including reduced hormone levels, improved uterine morphology, activation of BAX/Caspase-3 pathways, and strong docking to apoptotic targets. No clinical development has been reported. (https://www.tiprpress.com/ywpjyj/article/abstract/20240703)

Name: Pv SeroTAT
Developers: LSHTM
Indication: To detect infection with P. vivax in the preceding nine months for radical cure treatment
Health care facility level: IVDs for Health care facilities with clinical laboratories
Key features and challenges: A novel application is sero-test and treat, “seroTAT”. In seroTAT the presence of a serological marker of recent exposure to vivax serves as a proxy for hypnozoite carriage, suggesting the person is at risk for relapse and requires radical cure (assuming they are not G6PD deficient). Researchers, led by Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research and FIND, developing this approach estimate that in some settings up to half of vivax-infected individuals are asymptomatic with dormant liver stage parasites. While they are at risk for relapse, current diagnostics cannot detect them. To date, the serological biomarkers have achieved 80% sensitivity and specificity, the developers estimate that seroTAT interventions would identify 80% of vivax-infected people for radical cure. Compared to mass drug administration, overtreatment would be minimized (20%), reducing unnecessary treatments and side effects. In parallel to biomarker refinement, modelling, and studies, the researchers developing this approach have partnered with product developers to create POC versions of the test, including potentially a lateral flow assay.

Mechanism of action: It reverses the levels of related inflammatory and antioxidant markers.
Key features and challenges:
Pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) is a redox-active pyrroloquinoline compound characterized by oxo groups at the 4- and 5-positions and carboxy groups at the 2-, 7-, and 9-positions. It is produced by bacteria and occurs naturally in certain fruits and vegetables. PQQ has been described as a water-soluble vitamin-like compound with roles as a cofactor, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory agent.
Given that preeclampsia is associated with placental dysfunction, oxidative stress, and inflammatory activation—despite incomplete understanding of its pathogenesis—agents with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties have been explored as potential therapeutic candidates. PQQ has demonstrated such properties in preclinical investigations.
A 2022 study evaluated dietary supplementation with PQQ in an L-NAME–induced rat model of preeclampsia. Intraperitoneal administration of PQQ significantly improved clinical manifestations and pregnancy outcomes in PE-like rats. The intervention reversed alterations in inflammatory and oxidative stress markers. Mechanistic analyses suggested that PQQ exerted its protective effects through inhibition of the NF-κB pathway and activation of the Nrf2 antioxidant pathway.
(Source: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43032-021-00743-8)
Overall, current evidence for PQQ in PE/E is limited to preclinical animal models. While findings indicate potential anti-inflammatory and antioxidative benefits mediated through NF-κB–Nrf2 signalling pathways, clinical evidence in human populations is lacking.

Name: QDA-1
Developers: Brazilian Federal University of Pelotas, Universidade Federal de Pelotas (UFPEL)
Indication: Investigated for the treatment of Trichomoniasis.
Target: Disruption of purine nucleoside phosphorylase (TvPNP), lactate dehydrogenase (TvLDH), triosephosphate isomerase (TvTIM), and thioredoxin reductase (TvTrxR) pathways.
Mechanism of action: Binding at the active site of the T. vaginalis enzymes purine nucleoside phosphorylase, lactate dehydrogenase, triosephosphate isomerase, and thioredoxin reductase to inhibit enzymatic activities.
Key features and challenges:
QDA-1 (2,8-bis(trifluoromethyl) quinoline analogue) is a synthetic quinoline derivative investigated for antitrichomonal activity against Trichomonas vaginalis. Quinolines bearing trifluoromethyl substituents are associated with diverse pharmacological properties, including antimicrobial and antiparasitic effects.
A 2022 study conducted in vitro and in silico analyses of QDA-1 and reported complete reduction of trophozoite viability at 160 μM, with an IC₅₀ of 113.8 μM (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00436-022-07598-1). 
The compound inhibited parasite growth and increased reactive oxygen species production and lipid peroxidation after 24 hours of exposure, without inducing nitric oxide accumulation. Molecular docking analyses indicated favorable binding within the active sites of T. vaginalis enzymes including purine nucleoside phosphorylase, lactate dehydrogenase, triosephosphate isomerase, and thioredoxin reductase. QDA-1 exhibited moderate cytotoxicity in Vero cells (CC₅₀ = 247.4 μM), reducing viability by 36.7% at 200 μM, resulting in a modest selectivity index.
Key challenges include relatively high effective concentrations, limited selectivity margin, and the need for further mechanistic clarification. In vivo efficacy, pharmacokinetic profiling, and toxicity evaluation remain necessary prior to therapeutic consideration.
Overall, QDA-1 represents a synthetic quinoline scaffold with demonstrated in vitro activity against T. vaginalis. Further optimization and preclinical evaluation are required to determine its development potential.

Name: Quinagolide
Developers: Ferring Pharmaceuticals ; Novartis
Indication: Indicated for endometriosis pain and abnormal tissue growth
Mechanism of action: Dopamine D2 receptor agonists
Key features and challenges:
Quinagolide is a small-molecule dopamine D2-receptor agonist originally developed by Novartis for prolactinoma and hyperprolactinaemia. By stimulating pituitary D2 receptors, it suppresses prolactin secretion and reduces circulating prolactin levels. Quinagolide has been launched in multiple markets (including the EU, France, Canada, Hong Kong, Mexico, Russia, and South Africa), and clinical development has expanded into gynecological indications, including endometriosis, adenomyosis, and endometriosis-associated pain (https://adis.springer.com/drugs/800002555).
More recent development for endometriosis has focused on local administration via vaginal drug delivery systems (e.g., extended-release vaginal rings), aiming to support sustained exposure while potentially improving tolerability. In July 2021, Ferring Pharmaceuticals completed the Phase II proof-of-mechanism QLARITY trial evaluating a quinagolide extended-release vaginal ring, assessing reduction of lesions using high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging in women with endometriosis and/or adenomyosis (NCT03749109; https://adis.springer.com/trials/700301987
). In February 2022, Ferring completed the Phase II RQUEL trial evaluating efficacy, safety, and dose–response of sequentially administered quinagolide vaginal rings in women with moderate-to-severe endometriosis-related pain.
(NCT03692403; https://adis.springer.com/trials/700300363).
Key challenges include limited publicly available efficacy readouts from completed Phase II programs, uncertainty regarding the magnitude and durability of pain and lesion benefits, and the need to demonstrate clear differentiation versus established hormonal options. For vaginal ring delivery, acceptability, local tolerability, adherence, and consistency of drug release will be important considerations for real-world uptake. Further confirmatory studies with transparent reporting of clinical outcomes will be required to define regulatory and clinical positioning in endometriosis.
Overall, quinagolide represents a repurposed mechanism with a development shift toward extended-release vaginal ring delivery for endometriosis and endometriosis-associated pain. However, its clinical role remains dependent on publication of Phase II outcomes and subsequent confirmatory trials demonstrating meaningful benefit and tolerability.

Name: R-954
Developers: Brazilian Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ)
Indication: Indicated for the treatment of Endometriosis, including gestational loss.
Mechanism of action: Bradykinin B1 receptor antagonist.
Key features and challenges:
R-954 is a selective bradykinin B1 receptor antagonist investigated as a non-hormonal therapeutic candidate for endometriosis. Bradykinin signaling via the B1 receptor is associated with inflammation, pain sensitization, and angiogenesis—processes central to the establishment and progression of endometriotic lesions. Targeting the bradykinin B1 receptor therefore represents a strategy to modulate inflammatory and vascular components of the disease without directly suppressing ovarian hormone production.
A 2024 preclinical study evaluated R-954 in a murine model of endometriosis induced by autologous transplantation of uterine horn tissue (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0196978124001475?via%3Dihub). 
After lesion establishment, animals received either R-954 or progesterone for 15 consecutive days. Both treatments significantly reduced cyst size and weight and decreased inflammatory cell infiltrates and pro-inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-1β, interleukin-6, and tumor necrosis factor. Notably, R-954 uniquely reduced angiogenic markers such as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and its receptor, suggesting additional anti-angiogenic activity beyond progesterone. Importantly, R-954 did not disrupt the estrous cycle and was associated with reduced gestational losses, evidenced by fewer intermediate resorptions in pregnant females with endometriosis.
These findings indicate that R-954 exerts anti-inflammatory and anti-angiogenic effects while preserving reproductive cyclicity, suggesting potential advantages over hormonal therapies.
Key challenges include the limitation to animal models and absence of human clinical data. The long-term reproductive safety, systemic vascular effects, and potential off-target consequences of bradykinin receptor blockade require further evaluation. Translational studies are needed to determine pharmacokinetics, optimal dosing, and comparative efficacy relative to established hormonal therapies. While R-954 demonstrates promising non-hormonal disease-modifying effects in preclinical models, clinical validation is necessary before consideration for therapeutic use in women with endometriosis.

Name: RICAT (Radiometry Integrated Contrast Applied Therapy) system
Developers: H3PELVIC THERAPY SYSTEMS, INC.
Indication: Treatment of endometriosis pain
Mechanism of action: precise cooling and heating cycles to the pelvic region
Key features and challenges:
The RICAT (Radiometry Integrated Contrast Applied Therapy) system is a device-based technology developed by H3Pelvic Therapy Systems, Inc., designed to relieve pelvic pain through controlled thermal modulation. The system consists of a portable, tampon-sized thermal transfer probe incorporating heatpipe technology and smart radiometric sensors, combined with a water-circulating perineal membrane integrated into a seating platform. Passive microwave radiometry and embedded machine-learning algorithms are used to monitor and optimize real-time temperature delivery to deep pelvic tissues. The technology is being developed for pelvic pain associated with multiple conditions, including urinary tract infections, menstrual cramps, overactive bladder, interstitial cystitis/painful bladder syndrome, and endometriosis.
In 2023, a Phase I preclinical study was initiated to optimize and validate the RICAT system (https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10760002). 
The initial phase focuses on integrating radiometric sensors into the thermal probe and evaluating temperature-tracking accuracy compared with invasive needle sensors. The study involves ex vivo tissues and live porcine models undergoing vaginal or rectal cooling and warming cycles. The primary objective is to demonstrate consistent and effective thermal modulation of pelvic tissues, thereby supporting progression to human clinical trials, initially in patients with refractory interstitial cystitis.
Key challenges include the early, preclinical stage of development and the absence of human efficacy data in endometriosis-associated pain. Demonstrating safety, reproducibility, and clinically meaningful pain reduction in controlled human studies will be critical. Device acceptability, user comfort, regulatory pathway considerations, and integration into existing pelvic pain management strategies may also influence adoption.
Overall, the RICAT system represents a novel, non-pharmacologic thermal modulation approach targeting pelvic pain mechanisms relevant to endometriosis. However, clinical validation in human populations is required to establish its safety, efficacy, and therapeutic positioning.
